Job Description Summary
As a Calibration Apprentice, you will work within the Facilities Department, responsible for all site services across the Dowty Facilities. Calibration is the discipline that keeps every measurement — pressure, temperature, torque, dimension — accurate and traceable, giving us confidence that our instruments and controls are telling the truth. In an aerospace environment, that accuracy isn't optional: it's what stands between a component and catastrophic failure, so precision here has a direct line to flight safety.
The team's focus is 24/7 support of the facility, production areas, and production operations staff, ensuring Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) across our people and products.
The Department delivers effective planned calibration across all facilities and production equipment — from hands-on instrument and control systems to complex test rigs — performed both in-house and alongside external partners. As part of a small team operating in a fast-paced, highly regulated aerospace environment, you'll develop real technical expertise early, and you'll need to be self-motivated with the confidence to work autonomously.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Dowty, a GE Aerospace company is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for a wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft.

Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De Havilland Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J.

Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976, and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers.

Role Description

The primary purpose of the role is to undertake an apprenticeship 4yr program to achieve Calibration Technician status at Dowty.

This program will include attending college and participating in mandatory training courses to develop the technical and practical skills required for the role. Apprentices will gain hands-on experience in maintaining and improving advanced aerospace manufacturing equipment and systems. You will also complete online training as you progress through the apprenticeship.

You will be supported by your line manager, plus placement managers, mentors, and the wider apprentice network, to ensure you are meeting the requirements of your course and getting the most out of your apprenticeship.

Overview of the scheme

Embark on an exciting 4-year journey to kickstart your engineering career, with an additional 6 months dedicated to completing your End Point Assessment (EPA). This program will include attending Gloucestershire Engineering Training College to participating in mandatory training courses to develop the technical and practical skills required for the role. Apprentices will gain hands-on experience in maintaining and improving advanced aerospace manufacturing equipment and systems. In addition, online learning will be provided for the HNC component of learning by Teeside University. This apprenticeship program is designed to provide you with the perfect blend of academic learning and hands-on experience, setting you up for success in the aerospace industry.

Year 1: Building Your Foundation
Your first year will be spent full-time at college with GET Engineering Training, where you'll gain essential knowledge and skills to prepare you for the workplace. This immersive experience will lay the groundwork for your future success.

Year 2: Balancing College and Workplace Learning
In your second year, you'll attend college one day per week while spending the rest of your time in the workplace. This is your opportunity to apply what you've learned in a real-world setting, working alongside experienced professionals and contributing to meaningful projects.

Year 3:
Your third year will include the HNC Instrumentation course. You will study and progress onto the calibration of live equipment. The HNC study is online and done in conjunction with completing your level 3 study.

Year 4: Becoming a Key Team Member
Your final year is all about diving deeper into the workplace full-time. You'll take on more responsibilities, become an integral part of your department, and actively contribute to the apprenticeship community. During this time, you'll also have dedicated support to complete your HNC and EPA assignments.

At the completion of your studies, you will be awarded an HNC certificate of Instrumentation and Control Engineering.

Key Responsibilities

As an Apprentice you will learn to complete the following duties which is the expectation of a multiskilled technician.

- Planned Calibration & Maintenance: Learn to perform scheduled calibration checks and Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) on production equipment, instruments, and site services — ensuring measurement accuracy, reliability, and uptime.
- Equipment Repairs & Adjustment: Diagnose faults in instruments and control systems, carrying out repairs and recalibration with a "First Time Fix" methodology to minimise downtime.
- Documentation & Traceability: Record calibration results and equipment history in engineering computer systems, maintaining full traceability and completing required quality documentation to meet aerospace standards.
- Team Collaboration: Provide detailed handovers to engineering colleagues, ensuring calibration status and equipment condition are clearly communicated.
- Safety Compliance: Adhere to health and safety procedures, maintain a safe working environment, and support initiatives to enhance safety culture — recognising that accurate calibration is itself a critical safety control.
- Continuous Improvement: Participate in process and cost improvements, refining calibration methods and engineering practices to enhance equipment reliability and plant performance.
- Regulatory Awareness: Stay updated on current calibration standards and regulatory requirements (e.g. traceability to national/international standards) within your area of expertise.

Job Description Summary

Job Description

Job responsibilities require both independent, self-directed efforts, as well as team efforts working together with engineers and other technicians. You will work closely with our engineering and technical team to assemble, integrate, and test ground and flight systems for advanced aerospace applications. You will be responsible for the electronic and mechanical assembly, integration, checkout, and maintenance of prototype hardware and flight-ready systems. Applications for our development include advanced aircraft and propulsion systems, avionics and control systems, ground support equipment, as well as flight test instrumentation systems.

You will be expected to have strong attention to detail and the ability to work with both electronic components and mechanical assemblies. You will handle sensitive electronic equipment, precision mechanical parts, flight-critical hardware, and ground support systems. Some travel to external facilities (GE or customer sites) may be needed to support integration activities, system checkouts, or flight test campaigns.

The job will require moderate lifting of hardware up to 50 pounds, working in confined spaces, climbing ladders, and potentially working at elevated heights during system installation. In support of integration and testing activities, duties will include hardware preparation, system checkout procedures, working through detailed assembly and test checklists, and participating in integrated system tests. General housekeeping duties will also be expected, including the arrangement of tools and equipment, organization of parts and storage areas, electrostatic discharge (ESD) control, and overall work area cleanliness. Additionally, specialized cleaning and handling procedures shall be followed as required for flight hardware and clean-room environments.

Responsibilities:

- Perform electronic assembly including soldering, wire harnessing, circuit board installation, and connector assembly for ground and flight systems.
- Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and engineering specifications.
- Assemble and integrate mechanical components with electrical and electronic subsystems.
- Install, terminate, and test wiring and cable assemblies per IPC-A-620 and aerospace workmanship standards.
- Perform functional checkout and troubleshooting using multimeters, oscilloscopes, and test equipment.
- Conduct continuity checks, resistance measurements, and voltage/current testing to verify system functionality.
- Collaborate with engineers to resolve assembly issues and support root cause analysis.
- Document assembly procedures, test results, and as-built configurations per quality requirements.
- Perform rework and modifications per engineering change orders.
- Utilize hand tools, precision measuring instruments, crimping tools, torque wrenches, and power tools.
- Support integration of ground test systems and flight hardware, including instrumentation and sensor installation.
- Maintain organized work areas
- Perform periodic maintenance and calibration checks on test equipment and tools.
- Support flight system testing including pre-flight checkouts, ground operations, and post-flight inspections.

Requirements:

- High School Diploma or GED. Associate's degree or technical certification in electronics or avionics preferred.
- At least three (3) years of experience in electronic assembly, wire harnessing, and electro-mechanical integration. Aerospace or defense experience is highly desirable.
- Experience reading electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and assembly procedures.
- Proficiency in soldering, wire termination, connector assembly, and cable fabrication meeting IPC standards.
- Experience with electronic test equipment including multimeters, oscilloscopes, and data acquisition systems.
- Ability to obtain and maintain U.S. secret clearance. U.S. citizenship required.
- Ability to obtain and maintain ATF clearance.

Additional / Preferred Skills:

- Experience with avionics systems, flight instrumentation, or aircraft electrical systems.
- Familiarity with MIL-STD specifications and aerospace quality standards (AS9100).
- Proficiency with CAD software for viewing mechanical drawings and electrical schematics (e.g., Altium, NX).
- Experience with LabVIEW, MATLAB, or other data acquisition and analysis software.
- Experience with crimping and connector assembly for aerospace applications (Deutsch, Amphenol, circular connectors).
- Familiarity with composite materials handling and bonding techniques.
- Experience working in cleanroom or controlled environments.
- Familiarity with pneumatic and hydraulic systems integration.
- Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance.
- Previous experience supporting flight test operations or ground test campaigns.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation.

The base pay range for this position is $86,000 - $110,000 USD Annual. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on December 31st, 2026.

Job Description Summary

- Develop product cybersecurity processes for documentation, risk management, vulnerability recording, reporting, and incident response.
- Conduct comprehensive cybersecurity risk assessments on embedded products with varying levels of safety-criticality.
- Analyze hardware and software architectures for cybersecurity risks and feasibility of cybersecurity controls.
- Select and implement appropriate cybersecurity controls to mitigate embedded platform risks.
- Develop clear, precise technical requirements for cybersecurity implementations in embedded, real-time engine controllers and other aerospace embedded devices.

- Ensure timely completion of contract deliverables while maintaining quality standards.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including systems engineers, software developers, and program management.
- Develop and maintain embedded software and tools using programming languages such as C/C++, Python, and MATLAB/Simulink.

- Ensure that control systems and embedded software comply with industry standards and regulatory requirements.
- Lead LEAN initiatives to enhance system performance, reliability, and software quality.
- Own and conduct process improvements within Standard Work documents.
- Work with Product Line Leaders to understand product requirements and gather and translate customer requirements into executable product specifications.
- Provide timely communications on significant issues or developments.

The Engineering Test Technician will perform product testing and debug at both the complete-unit (“black box”) and circuit card assembly (CCA) levels. This individual will troubleshoot analog, digital, and microprocessor-based circuits; build, repair, and maintain test equipment; and support test-station setup and calibration.

- Experience performing product test and debug at the circuit board/CCA and/or complete-unit level.

Working at GE’s Jacksonville site offers exposure to advanced manufacturing processes, collaborative engineering teams, and opportunities for skill growth across electrical, mechanical and automation disciplines.

Our climate-controlled facility embraces diversity and career advancement, supported by 9 active employee resource groups.

Join GE and power innovation at our Jacksonville manufacturing site. We’re seeking a motivated Equipment Services Technician to maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize electro‑mechanical and electronic production/test equipment that keeps our operations running safely and efficiently.

What you’ll do

- Electrical experience: familiarity with 120/208/240/480 VAC systems and experience working with high‑voltage equipment.

- Mechanical and systems knowledge: pneumatics, hydraulics, vacuum and thermal systems; basic PLC understanding.

- Hands‑on troubleshooting and fabrication skills and effective written and verbal communication.

- Willingness to work extended/flexible hours to meet business needs.

postings.title: ESS Test Tech 2 (Lighting)
postings.location: Bohemia, New York, United States of America
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) aims to reveal any hidden defects and a high need of reliability, by applying accelerated environment stresses, such as vibrations or thermal cycling, to a product, using various testing procedures to accomplish this. ESS testing helps to prepare products for their real-world applications, so the testing conditions will often be the most extreme which the product may face in the real world. ESS tests can expose component failures. Thermal testing may find faults related to seal and gasket failures, insufficient wiring insulation and other component-level defects.

Job Description

At GE Aerospace in Bohemia, you will be part of a collaborative and diverse team that values your unique perspectives and innovative spirit. You will have the opportunity to work smarter, not harder, through our ongoing LEAN transformation. Your contributions will have a meaningful impact on millions of lives, and you will share in our sense of purpose and pride. If you are ready to elevate your future, come aboard and help us advance aviation technologies for today and tomorrow.

- Career Growth: GE isn’t just a great place to start your career—it’s a great place to expand and grow your career. Many entry-level employees grow into leadership roles in operations or other parts of the business. There are also opportunities to continue your career at GE in Bohemia or across the globe.

- Benefits: Our range of benefits includes health care starting on day one, 401 (k) savings plan with generous employer match, paid time off and more

- Education Assistance: GE encourages employees to continue their education and provides financial support to further employee learning.

- Work environment: GE Aerospace facility located in Islip, Long Island is dedicated to the design and manufacture of power conversion & control products, Battery systems, Lighting Controllers, Frequency Converters, Digital Control Products, Control Panels, Inverters, Power supplies and Advanced power conversion applications.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Testing may be conducted on the part level, assembly level or unit level.

- Combined Temperature and Electrodynamic Vibration

- Rapid Transition Rates

- Profile Execution for Extended Test Durations

- “Shake and Bake”

- Altitude

- Thermal Vacuum (TVAC)

These tests are conducted in dedicated environmental test chambers with advanced testing equipment

- Technicians place the product on vibration table testing X,Y,Z axis. Vibratory testing is more likely to uncover loose hardware and connectors, insufficiently torqued screw assemblies and weaknesses in switches and circuit breakers.

- Technicians place the product in an environmental test chamber based on product profiles and monitors temperature change. Other stimuli are applied to find defects in the product being tested.

- Test the product recording all successful tests and record all failures for further troubleshooting using specification data and schematics.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace:
Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Site Overview:

GE Aerospace Engine Services Malaysia (GEESM) in Subang plays a vital role in ensuring the safety and performance of aviation fleets every day. Established in 1997 as a Center of Excellence for CFM56 engines, GEESM has grown into a key hub of our global operations. It now services commercial aircraft engines, components, and accessories.

In 2018, we reaffirmed our continued commitment to Malaysia with a major US$80 million investment to further develop the Subang facility. This led to technological advancements that cemented GEESM’s role as a critical MRO hub for Malaysia's aviation industry. The MRO work on LEAP introduced the next chapter of engineering excellence for GEESM, making it the first such facility outside the United States for GE Aerospace.

Employing more than 700 highly skilled local professionals and providing MRO services to more than 50 airlines worldwide, GEESM continues to exceed our customers’ expectations. With our technical expertise and pioneering spirit, we elevate the flying experience to new heights.

Job Summary:

We are seeking interns to support the FLIGHT DECK team in driving workplace organization, visual management, and continuous improvement activities across operational areas. This role will provide hands-on support for daily execution and sustainment of FLIGHT DECK activities, including 5S, Daily Management, Standard Work, visual controls, data collection and analysis (including time and waste observations), and Kaizen event support.

This internship is a strong opportunity for students to gain practical exposure to lean operations, daily management, standard work, and continuous improvement in a MRO environment.

Role Overview:

- Support 5S, workplace organization, and visual management activities across the shopfloor

- Assist with setup and upkeep of Daily Management boards, ESN boards, standard work displays, flow lines and other lean initiatives.

- Conduct shopfloor process observations, time studies, and data collection and analysis to support improvement efforts.

- Help document Standard Work and identify opportunities to improve flow and reduce waste.

- Support Kaizen events and trainings through preparation, coordination, and follow-up activities.

- Track basic performance metrics and help organize information for FLIGHT DECK activities.

- Provide general team and administrative support as needed.

Ideal Candidate:

- Strong communicator who works well independently and engages confidently on the shop floor. Proactive, willing to learn, and enthusiastic about applying Lean principles to drive measurable improvements

- Good communication and teamwork skills

- Ability to manage multiple tasks and support a fast-paced operational environment

Required Qualifications:

- Currently pursuing a degree in Industrial, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Aerospace, or Materials Engineering

Financial Planning and Forecasting

- Develop and maintain financial models to forecast revenue, expenses, and cash flow for the LEAP product line.
- Lead the preparation of annual budgets, long-term financial plans, and quarterly forecasts.

Job Description Summary
In the 12-month Aeronautical/Aerospace/Mechanical Engineering - (Engines) Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience covering all aspects of engineering, from requirements analysis to product design to defining test specifications.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Engineering

Engineering is at the centre of what we do, and we are looking for talented, innovative engineers who can help us design and develop products for today, tomorrow, and in the future. If you are a dreamer, doer, and inventor who wants your voice to be heard and see your ideas take flight, this is the opportunity for you.

Roles and Responsibilities

In the 12-month Aeronautical/Aerospace/Mechanical Engineering - (Engines) Placement, you will gain hands-on experience across various teams and locations, contributing to the design, maintenance, and optimization of advanced jet engines.

While responsibilities vary depending on the team and location, you could engage in activities such as engine work scoping, tooling development, repair industrialization, cost optimization, and customer support.

You could collaborate with cross-functional teams, apply lean principles, and develop technical expertise in areas like gas turbine fundamentals, engine architecture, and shop production methods.

This placement offers structured training, mentorship, and opportunities to work on impactful projects that support GE Aerospace's mission of delivering world-class aviation solutions.

Placement Options based on locations

Cardiff:

GE9X Product Support Engineering (PSE): Focused on pre-Engine in Service (EIS) readiness, ensuring overhaul shop preparation, tooling development, service bulletin updates, and technical support for customers. Students will gain exposure to the overhaul process, technical data collection, and lean project implementation.

Engineering Team (Operations): Supporting jet engine overhaul for GE90 and CFM engine types, with responsibilities including engine work scoping, repair specification implementation, cost optimization, and production support. Students will develop strong customer relations and contribute to transitioning MRO processes to a digital environment.

Powerplant, Repair, SPO & NPI Engineering

Caledonian- GEnx Customer Technical Programs (CTP): Supporting the Strategic Powerplant Engineering team in tooling development, hardware condition review, repair industrialization, and work scope escalation management. Students will work with cross-functional teams to enhance serviceability limits and introduce new repair methods.

This placement provides a unique opportunity to develop technical, analytical, and collaborative skills while contributing to the future of aviation.

You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.

If you are passionate about Aerospace/Aeronautical/Mechanical Engineering, we would love to hear from you.

This opportunity is offered in our Cardiff and Caledonian (Prestwick, Scotland) sites, during the process we will ask you to share your location preferences.

GE Aerospace Wales specialises in the maintenance, repair and overhaul of a range of commercial jet engines. The facility, based in Nantgarw, just north of Cardiff, occupies over 1.2 million square feet of workshop space and has two state-of-the-art aircraft engine test facilities, along with a significant repair capability – known as Component Repair Wales.

The site has the capability to provide maintenance, repair and overhaul services for a range of engine types – including the world’s most powerful commercial aircraft engine the GE90-115B and the world’s most popular commercial engine the CFM56.

As one of the largest commercial aircraft engine maintenance facilities in the world, with annual sales of over $2bn, the business works with over 90 customers worldwide, including Emirates, TUI, Lufthansa, Delta, United, ANA and British Airways.

In 2017, the Wales site was selected as the Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility of choice for the GE9X; which will become the world’s largest and most fuel-efficient jet engine when it launches into service. The business will benefit from a £5m investment from the Welsh Government to support the total £20m investment put forward by the business, to equip and upskill the facility to be ready to maintain the GE9X fleet when it enters service on the new Boeing 777X aircraft.

The Wales team places a strong focus on providing career opportunities for talented individuals. Our apprenticeship, internship and work experience opportunities have been built to ensure the long-term success of our business by developing the next generation of technical, engineering and problem-solving talent.

GE Aerospace Caledonian is a purpose-built aircraft engine overhaul facility, adjacent to Glasgow Prestwick International Airport. The Caledonian site was officially opened in 1980 and has since grown into a centre of excellence for Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) of CF6 & GEnx engine types. After each overhaul, the engines undergo intensive performance testing on site in our bespoke test cell, before returning to our global customer base ready for service.

Our vastly experienced and innovative workforce are passionate in the contribution towards the training of future engineers, leaders and surrounding talent in our organisation. At GE Caledonian, our Apprentices (Foundation, Modern & Graduate), XLP, OMLP and interns are key members of our team helping achieve the challenges of tomorrow. They continuously develop new skills to keep up with the pace of change in the Aviation Industry and become comfortable working in this ever-challenging environment which thrives on embracing change.

Our diverse team have a strong foothold in the local community, proactively seeking new volunteering opportunities to give back and deliver on our corporate responsibility. We have a dedicated affinity group on site who facilitate opportunities to the wider team, creating an inclusive culture we can all be proud of.

This placement role is an intended pipeline for our Graduate Aerospace Engineer Programme which is based at our Cardiff site. Towards the end of the placement year, we will open graduate applications for our current placement students with an aim to secure a role prior to the end of their placement year.

Meaning, you can head back into your final year at university with a graduate job offer in hand. All you need to do is secure a 2,1 degree or above!

On this programme, you will learn and develop your skills and capability through working with professional engineers on projects that ensure continuous improvements and growth to the business.

We have different types of roles in this area; here is a brief snapshot into each:

Digital Technology (Cardiff) - you will play a key part in developing a Digital Toolset to drive productivity within the business functions. You will lead various projects utilising applications from the GE Toolset and new Analytics Tools. You will partner with these business functions to understand requirements and translate these into Operational Tools.

Digital Technology (Caledonian) - Development of prototype local applications for SQDIP improvements.

DT Technology and Operations Team (Cheltenham) - providing support for iPhone and iPad devices, including setup, upgrades, compliance, and issue resolution. You will manage requests for new network port installations, remote access, and GUEST WiFi changes, while assisting users with supply chain applications. Responsibilities also include managing a Raspberry Pi-based signage solution, covering procurement, build, and configuration of devices. Project activities may involve supporting application deployments and upgrades, as well as managing small-scale equipment deployments and installations.

Digital Technology (Dowty) - improving how the business uses data and digital technologies to drive better decisions and performance. You will help enhance data maturity by improving data quality, structure, standardization, governance, and accessibility, and work with business and digital teams to understand reporting needs and develop dashboards and visualizations for key metrics. The position involves gathering, cleaning, validating, and analyzing data to support operational and strategic decisions, while identifying opportunities where AI can create business value and building clear business cases for adoption. You will research digital and AI trends and best practices, help evaluate AI use cases for impact, feasibility, risks, and data readiness, and lead or coordinate a digital technology project from scope definition through milestone tracking and stakeholder communication. In addition, you will support cross-functional collaboration to ensure solutions align with user needs, prepare presentations and updates for reviews, and contribute to process improvements that enhance efficiency, visibility, and decision-making.

Cyber Security (Cheltenham) - you will work across five key cyber security areas: Intelligence, Enterprise Vulnerability Management, Insider Threat, External Threat, and Digital Forensics. The student will spend two months in each area, gaining an understanding of daily operations by working with key staff and delivering a small project to showcase what they have learned. In the final two months, the student can choose one of these areas to focus on. Throughout the placement, they will receive training and hands-on experience with cyber tools used by the UK Cyber Team, explore topics aligned to their course such as malware analysis and networking, and have opportunities to participate in Cyber Capture the Flag events during the year.

Engineering Leadership (Cheletenham) - data and digital - focused role embedded in engineering, closely linked to supply chain and factory operations. Reporting to the Engineering Executive Leader, you will support major initiatives such as Product Cost Hoshin Kanri, Defect PSR, and zero-defect improvement activities by using data analytics, digital tools, and AI/advanced analytics to analyse product cost and defect data, build dashboards and digital solutions, and drive lean, data-driven process and quality improvements. Key responsibilities include applying statistical and data science techniques to product cost data, creating visual dashboards (Tableau, Power BI, Excel), exploring AI methods (predictive models, clustering, anomaly detection), and collaborating with engineering, supply chain, IT/digital, and cross-functional teams. You will also develop defect analytics tools, use AI/ML for defect pattern recognition and risk scoring, participate in Genba at the factory to link digital insights to real processes, and help shape data pipelines, performance metrics, and visual management that support continuous improvement in Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost.

This placement is perfect for students who want to grow their skills and gain valuable experience in digital technology.

You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.

The site has the capability to provide maintenance, repair and overhaul services for a range of engine types – including the world’s most powerful commercial aircraft engine the GE90-115B and the world’s most popular commercial engine the CFM56.

As one of the largest commercial aircraft engine maintenance facilities in the world, with annual sales of over $2bn, the business works with over 90 customers worldwide, including Emirates, TUI, Lufthansa, Delta, United, ANA and British Airways.

Total Reward

As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs.

- Non-contributory Pension

- Life Assurance

- Group income protection

- Private medical cover

- Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible options to buy or sell

As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process.

If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com.

Please note our applications will close on Saturday 31st October but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too.

Security Clearance

Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS.

UK Security Clearance

UK Security Clearance (SC) may be required and maintained for some of our placement roles. Due to the nature of work, some of these roles are restricted to candidates who are a British National, or a dual National where one of the dual nationalities is British subject to any restrictions. Mechanical Design & Analysis (Cheltenham) - This hardware placement sits within the mechanical design area and combines both mechanical design and analysis work, typically across several projects or 1–2 larger programmes. The types of products you could work on include power distribution units, controllers, and display systems, providing broad exposure to the hardware product lifecycle.

Job Description Summary

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Roles and Responsibilities

In the 12-month Programme Management Placement offers diverse roles within the function, with responsibilities tailored to the specific needs of different teams. While all roles focus on program management, customer support, and operational efficiency, tasks will vary based on team priorities and projects.

Responsibilities may include:

- Coordinating customer requests such as RFQs and purchase orders, ensuring deadlines are met through collaboration with supply chain and engineering teams, preparing customer order books, facilitating client calls, and ensuring high satisfaction and timely delivery.

- Support Program Management Reviews (PMRs) by managing calendars, preparing agendas, and tracking actions.

- Leading process improvement projects to enhance operational efficiency, implementing Lean principles, and analysing operational data to create performance metrics that drive team focus on strategic priorities.

- Cross-functional collaboration is a key aspect of the role, working closely with Operations, Sourcing, Engineering, and Quality teams to meet customer and business objectives. Some teams may focus on facilities and maintenance, including asset reviews, day-to-day operations, contractor control, and long-term projects to support stakeholders.

We have opportunities within:

- Field Services (Dowty) - managing internal metrics, financials, materials, pricing models, and logistics, with broad exposure to satellite sites and international field locations. The role involves tracking KPIs (such as turnaround times, schedule adherence, utilisation, and cost performance), maintaining dashboards and reports, and supporting root cause analysis of performance issues. You will assist with financial tracking (revenue, costs, margins), support pricing model updates, help manage materials data, and contribute to cost analysis for continuous improvement. On the operational side, you will coordinate logistics information, support planning for field activities, and maintain documentation so stakeholders stay informed. The role requires close collaboration with Programmes, Finance, Operations, and Logistics, including supporting cross-functional reviews and small improvement projects in reporting, data quality, and process flow. The placement offers end-to-end exposure to field service operations, practical experience in metrics, financial and logistics coordination, and development of professional communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.

- Facilitates & Maintenance Projects (Caledonian) - learning maintenance management and continuous improvement in a business operations environment, covering preventive and reactive maintenance, preventive maintenance planning, compliance, sustainability projects, and environmental monitoring and gap analysis. Monitoring performance metrics, identifying improvement opportunities and developing project management skills through small- to medium-scale projects. The role requires adapting to different people and environments daily, understanding departmental challenges to set maintenance priorities, communicating with various stakeholders and responding to critical needs, and learning from experienced staff to improve existing processes and work-scopes. Also working with suppliers and contractors during preventive maintenance to ensure high safety standards, gain exposure to shift supervision and maintenance management, and collaborate with internal and external resources on sustainment and environmental improvement projects.

- Military Platforms (Cheltenham) - broad range of program management, customer support, order management, and cross-functional business improvement activities within a military-focused organisation. The role is designed to give the intern practical experience in managing internal special projects, supporting customer engagement, and becoming familiar with program management practices, procedures, internal systems, and standard work. The placement will work closely with stakeholders, customers, and colleagues across multiple functions, while contributing to business-focused projects, driving actions to closure, presenting findings and recommendations, and developing communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

- BizJet Portfolio (Cheltenham) - you will gain exposure to the complete program and product lifecycle, from new product introduction through to repair and overhaul services. The programs team you will join is a dynamic and growing portfolio, offering a strong opportunity to contribute to day‑to‑day program activities and develop core program management skills. Key activities include reviewing customer purchase orders and supporting the Program Team in managing the product orderbook, ensuring alignment between customer portals and internal order management systems. You will support sales and operational review meetings through orderbook management and engagement with key stakeholders involved in demand changes. You will help with obsolescence management by developing regular reviews with key functions, monitoring stock run‑out dates, and improving communication with other programs where obsolescence risk is shared. You will act as a “voice of the customer”, supporting communication between internal teams and the customer, engaging with customers to help secure invoice payment in support of cash targets, and helping to organise and support program review meetings with customers.

- OE Value Stream Programs (Dowty) - focuses on planning, coordinating, and delivering manufactured spare parts to ensure reliable aftermarket support. The role owns the integrated production and delivery plan for defined part families, aligning production and materials with customer demand and business priorities, and applying a structured operating model to meet Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost objectives. Working cross‑functionally with materials planning, manufacturing, quality, sourcing, logistics, and customer‑facing teams, the role manages production schedules, monitors performance, addresses risks and issues, and keeps customers informed through clear, proactive communication on delivery status, changes, and recovery plans. It combines operational planning, data‑driven performance management, and customer relationship management to improve delivery reliability and overall supply chain effectiveness.

- Programme Management Office (Cheltenham) - supporting the successful delivery of complex projects from early bid and concept stages through to closure. The PMO Project Controller is responsible for managing budgets and schedules using standardised tools, maintaining integrated project plans, and providing analysis to identify and mitigate cost and schedule risks. The role serves as a key point of contact for project management tools and practices, coaching project and technical leaders and performing earned value analysis to support informed decision-making. It also supports structured change and risk management processes, including preparing change documentation, participating in risk and opportunity reviews, and ensuring decisions are clearly recorded. In addition, the PMO Project Controller contributes to accurate project forecasting and helps coordinate resource plans across multiple teams to ensure projects are appropriately staffed and controlled.

- Programme Management (Cheltenham) - This role offers a strong development opportunity in program management best practices by applying daily management and lean principles across all workstreams of one of our programmes. The individual will be responsible for maintaining robust document control across NPI, production execution and aftermarket, coordinating actions with the integrated program team (IPT) following tollgate reviews and key meetings, and ensuring all program risks and opportunities are captured and managed in the digital thread tool. The role also includes monitoring and reporting touch labour and material performance against targets, identifying opportunities to eliminate non‑value‑added work using lean principles and project management principles. Through these activities, the individual will gain hands-on experience in quality assurance, QMS, risk management, and end-to-end program execution.

You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. postings.description:
Job Description Summary
In the 12-month Software Engineering Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills and experience in covering all aspects of software engineering from software design and integration to testing.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Engineering

Engineering is at the centre of what we do, and we are looking for talented, innovative engineers who can help us design and develop products for today, tomorrow, and in the future. If you are a dreamer, doer, and inventor who wants your voice to be heard and see your ideas take flight, this is the opportunity for you.

Roles and Responsibilities

In the 12-month Software Engineering Placement, you'll gain invaluable skills by working as part of a team during part of (or multiple parts) the Development Life Cycle. Depending on your skillset and role requirements, you will develop your programming languages skills in (but not limited to) Java, C, C++, C#, Python, Raspberry Pi and/or Arduino.

You could be analyzing requirements, designing an application, or defining a test specification or supporting configuration management, database development and system monitoring, engaging with internal and external customers and third-party vendors.

We have several different types of roles in different teams:

- On Wing Technology (Bristol) - developing intuitive, responsive user interfaces for aerospace applications using modern web technologies. You will design and implement user-facing features with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, working closely with UI/UX designers to turn wireframes into high-quality code and ensure designs are technically feasible. The role involves collaborating with back-end developers to integrate front-end components, participating in agile practices (sprint planning, reviews, retrospectives), engaging in code reviews and best practices, troubleshooting and resolving issues, and staying current with emerging software development trends and technologies.

- Software Engineering (Cheltenham) - use good engineering practice and AI tools to improve project outcomes across Quality, Delivery, and Cost: You strengthen code quality by following agreed coding standards, actively participating in code reviews, and suggesting maintainability improvements that help reduce long-term cost. You contribute to continuous improvement by engaging in team retrospectives and capturing changes that lower defects and delays, improving both Quality and Delivery. You build systems thinking by joining cross-team projects, learning how upstream and downstream changes affect Delivery, Quality, and Cost. You explore and share advances in tools, frameworks, and AI for engineering, focusing on options that improve Quality, accelerate Delivery, and reduce Cost. You use AI-assisted tools to generate and refine test ideas and documentation, validating outputs to improve Quality while reducing Cost and effort. You also apply AI to summarise technical articles and documentation for the team, helping spread knowledge quickly and efficiently, supporting Quality and Delivery at low Cost.

- Software Tools (Cheltenham) - maintains, supports, and improves the engineering toolchains used across NPI projects. You will be supported by experienced engineers and a strong learning and continuous improvement culture as you learn the toolchains, contribute to support and enhancement work, and develop through hands-on projects, mentorship, and training. Key responsibilities include optimising day-to-day use of engineering tools (issue triage, root cause analysis, resolution), implementing and testing enhancements to improve usability, reliability, and performance, and translating stakeholder requests into requirements, design changes, implementation, and verification. You will document configurations, changes, known issues, and test evidence according to engineering policies, prepare and present technical findings and status updates, participate in cross-functional initiatives and continuous improvement activities, and provide timely updates on risks, issues, and progress to support short-term planning and unblock delivery.

- Test Systems (Cheltenham) - you will train up be safe in Lab and Production areas, learn full software development lifecycle processes and adhere to them. Track and deliver software releases on time & identify improvements to projects.

- Engineering Operations Power portfolio (Cheltenham) - provide support across digital transformation activities, helping to drive automation, simplification, and optimisation of business processes. Working with the Business Change Manager, you will help run an effective operating rhythm by preparing reports and dashboards, managing digital reporting tools, dashboards, and web apps, and supporting the implementation of new digital tools. You will track and administer digital transformation projects and other improvement activities, document business data sources, and contribute to defining a future data analytics strategy for Engineering Operations. The role also involves engaging cross-functionally, facilitating process reviews and improvements, and building strong relationships across the organisation.

You will be guided by structured goals and objectives and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.

This opportunity is offered in our Bristol (Bristol Robotic Services) and Cheltenham sites, during the process we will ask you to share your location and role preferences.

GE Aerospace, Bristol Robotic Services (BRS) is a small tightknit office located in Bristol, South West England. We are a team of ~50 talented, dedicated and hardworking employees who collaborate to solve very interesting challenges in the aerospace industry. Every day at BRS is unique; you will be presented with exciting technical problems to solve and be given the space to innovate bespoke solutions. Given the small size of the company, it is very clear to see the impact your work makes, so if you are someone who grabs opportunity with both hands, you will find your time here very rewarding.

We are looking for high-energy, self-motivated individuals with the vision to help carry our business forward.  The work is academically rigorous, intellectually demanding, and requires exceptional problem-solving, communication, leadership and interpersonal skills. That being said, we are a very collaborative bunch so we don’t need you to be an expert in everything, we have experts here who will mentor and coach you into developing the skills you need.

Our offices are in Bristol in the South West of England – an area fast becoming a major centre for robotics. Job Description Summary
Depot Subject Matter Expert provides depot-level technical expertise for T700/CT7 engine maintenance, repair, inspection, assembly/disassembly, troubleshooting, and test activities. This role supports both hands-on shop execution and quality/engineering-focused evaluation of maintenance activities, ensuring work is performed in accordance with technical directives, approved procedures, and operational requirements. This role also helps develop workforce capability by coaching and training customer personnel on quality systems, supporting documentation, workstation development, heavy machine operation, and technical discipline.

Job Description

Role Overview

GE Aerospace is seeking a T700/CT7 (Turboshaft) Depot Subject Matter Expert - Shop Floor to support hands-on depot execution for T700/CT7 engines, modules, and components. This role is ideal for a practical engine maintenance professional who brings deep shop knowledge, strong technician instincts, and a commitment to safe, disciplined execution. You will help drive daily maintenance activity across inspection, disassembly, assembly, tooling, support equipment, and test stand support while coaching personnel and helping the team solve issues quickly and effectively. This role is full time, on-site at customer facility located in Deblin, Poland.

Key Responsibilities

· Support depot maintenance execution for T700-GE-701C/D, CT7-2E1 and CT7-8E engines, modules, and components across inspection, disassembly, assembly, repair support, and final preparation activities.

· Assist with removal, installation, inspection, repairs, and modifications using approved maintenance procedures and sound workmanship practices.

· Train the customer and support engine and module disassembly and assembly activities with focus on task discipline, cleanliness, hardware accountability, and safe execution.

· Support movement, handling, preservation, storage, and transportation preparation of engines and engine modules as required by depot operations.

· Assist with installation and removal of engines on test stands and support engine operation, evaluation, and testing activities with the appropriate customer teams.

· Inspect, maintain, and train customer on engine ground support equipment and related support equipment needed for maintenance execution.

· Assist in selection and use of special tools, hand tools, fixtures, and test equipment correctly, and help reinforce proper use, care, and readiness of shop assets.

· Provide hands-on coaching and on-the-job training to customer personnel to strengthen technician capability and execution consistency.

· Help identify and resolve shop floor issues involving tooling, equipment readiness, workflow interruptions, or technical execution barriers.

· Work closely with GE internal and customer operations, quality, and engineering teams to maintain safe, efficient, and compliant maintenance flow.

Basic Qualifications

· Demonstrated experience in T700/CT7 engine maintenance, depot operations, or closely related turboshaft engine shop activity.

· Hands-on experience with engine or module inspection, assembly, disassembly, and maintenance execution in a controlled shop environment.

· Ability to interpret technical manuals, drawings, schematics, and maintenance instructions and apply them accurately on the shop floor.

· Experience supporting troubleshooting, repair activity, or maintenance task completion on turbine engines or related systems.

· Experience using tooling, fixtures, support equipment, and test equipment relevant to engine depot maintenance and handling activity.

· Working knowledge of safe work practices, tool control, hardware accountability, and procedural compliance in maintenance operations.

· Ability to provide effective on-the-job training, technician coaching, and practical execution guidance.

Preferred Qualifications

· Experience supporting shop operations, production flow, military or depot sustainment programs, or complex maintenance environments utilizing FLIGHT DECK or similar lean operating system.

· Background in test operations, equipment readiness, engine handling, or support equipment maintenance.

· Demonstrated tooling discipline and ability to reinforce efficient, organized, and repeatable work practices.

· Experience working within matrix operations, quality, engineering, and support functions to remove barriers and solve issues quickly.

· Ability to contribute to continuous improvement, daily execution rhythm, and practical shop floor problem solving.

· Experience leading by example in workmanship, safe execution, technician development, and task accountability.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means helping the customer depot team execute hands-on engine maintenance with strong safety, quality, and workflow discipline. You will bring practical shop leadership, support reliable use of tools and equipment, coach technicians in the moment, and help keep engine and module work moving efficiently from receiving, inspection, and teardown through test and final preparation. Customer will take away a continuous improvement mindset, with the ability to properly utilize and implement FLIGHT DECK tools in response to shop identified concerns.

EEO

GE Aerospace is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

Job Description Summary
Colibrium Additive is seeking a Global Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Leader to establish, scale, and continuously improve a risk-based EHS program across our global operations. This leader will set the strategic direction for EHS, build a strong culture of care and accountability, and use data, technology, and cross-functional partnership to keep our people safe and our operations compliant, resilient, and future-ready. The role suits a strategic and hands-on leader with deep EHS expertise, strong influencing skills, and a track record of driving measurable improvement in complex, multi-site industrial environments — including those with additive manufacturing and metal powder hazards.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Governance

Develop, implement, and sustain a global EHS strategy, policies, and standards aligned with business priorities and regulatory requirements.

Establish governance mechanisms to ensure consistent EHS expectations, accountability, and execution across all sites.

Risk Management & Operational Excellence

Lead enterprise and site-level risk assessments, EHS audits, and management system reviews; prioritize corrective and preventive actions to reduce risk.

Implement sustainable controls for key hazards relevant to the business, including high-risk operations such as metal powder/process safety.

Use EHS data, analytics, and leading indicators to identify trends, predict risk, and prioritize resources — moving the organization from reactive to predictive safety management.

Culture, Leadership & Capability Building

Drive a proactive, no-blame EHS culture through visible leadership, engagement routines, and reinforcement of safe behaviors at all levels — one where employees feel psychologically safe raising concerns, reporting near-misses, and stopping unsafe work.

Coach, develop, and enable site EHS leaders and coordinators; ensure consistent application of standards and effective local ownership.

Design and deploy effective EHS training programs to build competence, awareness, and compliance, leveraging digital and e-learning tools where they improve reach and retention.

Support employee wellbeing initiatives that address physical and mental health, recognizing wellbeing as integral to a sustainable safety culture.

Performance Management & Reporting

Define, monitor, and communicate EHS performance metrics, including metrics tied to sustainability and ESG commitments; analyze trends and translate insights into targeted improvement actions.

Provide clear reporting for leadership reviews, including progress versus goals, systemic risks, and improvement roadmap status.

Incident Management & Learning

Lead incident investigations and root cause analyses; ensure timely, transparent closure and verification of corrective actions.

Drive organizational learning by sharing insights, improving leading indicators, and focusing on prevention-oriented actions.

Cross-Functional Partnership & External Awareness

Partner with Production, Engineering, Service, HR, and Legal to embed EHS and ergonomics considerations into core business processes, change management, facility planning, and investment decisions.

Maintain awareness of regulatory changes, emerging risks (including those tied to new materials, automation, and additive manufacturing processes), and industry best practices, keeping the business compliant and proactive.

Build and maintain an active network with EHS colleagues across GE Aerospace and the broader industry to share best practices and accelerate adoption of proven approaches.

Required Qualifications

- Education: Bachelor's degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Health, Engineering, or a related technical field from an accredited institution, or equivalent qualification. Advanced degree preferred.
- Experience: Multiple years of progressive EHS leadership experience, ideally in a global and/or multi-site manufacturing environment and/or field services organization.
- Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of current EHS regulations, standards, and industry best practices, along with the judgment to apply them pragmatically.
- Language: Business fluency in English required; German and/or French is a plus given the site footprint.
- Travel: Ability and willingness to travel approximately 30%, with flexibility for more during peak project periods.

Preferred Qualifications / Desired Characteristics

- Certifications: CSP, CIH, NEBOSH, or equivalent professional EHS certification strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated success building and scaling EHS programs across complex operations and driving measurable improvement in safety outcomes.
- Domain expertise in high-hazard operations, including additive manufacturing environments, metal powder hazards, and process safety management.
- Comfort using EHS data platforms, dashboards, and digital tools to drive decisions and reporting.
- Strong influencing, communication, and stakeholder management skills across all organizational levels, from the shop floor to senior leadership.
- Analytical, structured problem-solving ability, with a track record of translating data into prioritized, actionable improvement plans.

Colibrium Additive is committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone is treated with respect and given equal opportunity to succeed. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

postings.description:
Job Description Summary
The Information Security Manager (ISM) is the primary cybersecurity focal at the site. This role is responsible for implementing, sustaining, monitoring, and auditing cybersecurity controls; ensuring compliance with global, regional, and contractual requirements (e.g., CMMC, EASA Part-IS); and promoting a strong cybersecurity culture across the facility. The ISM bridges OT, IT, and cybersecurity, acts as first-level approver for security-related changes, and partners with site leadership and Digital Technology (DT) to continuously improve the site’s cyber posture.

Job Description

Company Overview:

Working at GE Aerospace means you are bringing your unique perspective, innovative spirit, drive, and curiosity to a collaborative and diverse team working to advance aerospace for future generations. If you have ideas, we will listen. Join us and see your ideas take flight!

Site Overview:

GE Aerospace Engine Services Malaysia (GEESM) in Subang is a key part of our global maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) network, supporting the service of commercial aircraft engines, components, and accessories with world-class technical expertise. Established in 1997 as a Center of Excellence for CFM56 engines, the site has continued to grow, including becoming GE Aerospace’s first LEAP MRO facility outside the U.S. We are also expanding our footprint in Malaysia with a new LEAP engine MRO facility in Sepang! Expected to open in late 2026, adding advanced capabilities, new technology, and opportunities to support the next generation of aviation maintenance.

Employing more than 700 highly skilled local professionals and providing MRO services to more than 50 airlines worldwide, GEESM continues to exceed our customers’ expectations. With our technical expertise and pioneering spirit, we elevate the flying experience to new heights.

Role Overview:

Cybersecurity Implementation & Monitoring:

- Lead the Site Cyber Implementation Team to deploy and sustain the Cyber Playbook and other corporate cyber standards.

- Track site-level cyber activities and risks (e.g., CMMC/IA defects, EASA Part-IS, vulnerabilities, endpoint monitoring coverage) and maintain a site cyber action plan.

- Report cybersecurity metrics in Shop MOR/Daily Management and provide updates to site and DT leadership.

- Act as first-level approver for security-related change management requests (e.g., firewall rules, ports, OT/IT connectivity), ensuring changes are risk-assessed, documented, and compliant.

Auditing and Compliance:

- Ensure the site complies with applicable cybersecurity regulations, standards, and contractual requirements (global, regional, and customer-specific).

- Partner with relevant functions to support customer audits, regulatory inspections, and technical reviews.

- Assist with root cause analysis, corrective actions, and clarifications during and after external and internal audits.

Incident Management:

- Serve as the local support for cybersecurity incidents, coordinating with the Global Incident Response Team within Cyber and DT for triage, containment, and recovery.

- Support incident response readiness, including communication of roles, escalation paths, and participation in drills.

- Contribute to post-incident reviews and drive implementation of corrective and preventive actions.

Cybersecurity Culture and Continuous Improvement:

- Actively promote cybersecurity rules and best practices within the facility.

- Conduct presentations and training sessions for various departments to enhance cybersecurity awareness and ownership.

- Use appropriate communication channels to disseminate cybersecurity information and expectations.

- Engage with shop floor, OT, and cross-functional stakeholders (Operations, Quality, EHS, Compliance, Facilities, BISOs, DT) to embed cybersecurity into daily operations and projects.

Ideal Candidate:

- The ideal candidate is having strong understanding of cybersecurity risk management in large enterprise environment. Having spent time managing audits and ensuring cyber controls are in place and working effectively.

Required Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

- 5-7 years of experience in operational technology (OT) and cybersecurity, preferably in manufacturing, industrial, or critical infrastructure environments.

- Strong knowledge of regulatory and standards requirements at regional and global levels (e.g., CMMC, EASA Part-IS, IA, and contractual cybersecurity obligations).

- Proven ability to lead projects and manage cybersecurity initiatives, coordinating cross-functional teams and driving actions to closure.

- Ability to travel 30% (once per month) to the site to ensure cybersecurity controls are operating effectively.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and explain complex topics to non-technical audiences.

Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

Chez GE Aérospatial, nous faisons progresser les technologies aéronautiques d’aujourd’hui et de demain. Job Description Summary
The Integrated Manufacturing Assembly & Test FP&A Leader manages planning, analysis, and reporting for the consolidated view of Part Families and IMAT as an aggregate. This leader should support the Integrated Manufacturing Assembly & Test CFO by enabling IMAT-wide standard work and efficient financial processes. This role will provide strategic financial insights and support decision-making processes. This leader will work directly with the entire IMAT General Manager and IMAT Staff to enable operational performance and implement strategies that align with business objectives.

In addition to FP&A responsibilities, a critical part of this role is directly supporting special projects across the IMAT Shops, including, but not limited to Business Development opportunities, key acquisition integrations, ERP implementation projects, and various other IMAT-level strategic initiatives. This role will be responsible for leading and managing key efforts in these special projects to support the IMAT division.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

As the Integrated Manufacturing Assembly & Test FP&A leader you will:

- Financial Planning, Reporting, and Analysis: Lead Part Family and Shop finance teams in executing planning and reporting cycles, delivering comprehensive financial reports with variance analysis, and driving process automation to enhance transparency and streamline reporting.
- Forecasting and Risk Management: Manage planning, forecasting, and pacing activities by leveraging data insights and operational expertise to identify material variances, mitigate risks, and capitalize on opportunities, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial results.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration and Communication: Foster engagement with cross-functional teams to effectively communicate financial positions, analyze operating results, and provide actionable insights to support strategic decision-making.
- Operational Reviews and Consolidation: Own the consolidation and analysis of financial data for IMAT’s Monthly Operating Reviews (MORs) and Weekly Operating Reviews (WORs), ensuring alignment with organizational goals and priorities.
- Strategic Planning and Reporting: Lead planning, forecasting, and pacing efforts for IMAT HQ, utilizing data-driven approaches to articulate material variances, risks, and opportunities. Support the IMAT CFO in preparing presentations and materials for key reviews, including MORs, WORs, Wrap Reviews, Budget, Strategy, and Board of Directors meetings.
- Continuous Improvement Through FLIGHT DECK: Apply FLIGHT DECK methodologies to drive continuous improvement across all financial processes within IMAT, fostering a lean and efficient operating model.
- Special Projects and Strategic Initiatives: Collaborate across shops and part families to lead or support special projects, including developing business cases, conducting due diligence for business development, integrating new sites and ERPs, and spearheading IM-level cross-functional initiatives.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in finance or accounting from an accredited university
- 6+ years of FP&A/Supply Chain Finance experience

Desired Characteristics

- Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
- Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects cross-functionally
- Experience with shop/supply chain finance
- Proven track record of driving financial performance
- Evidence of leveraging FLIGHT DECK to improve processes
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex financial data and provide actionable insights.
- Strong business acumen and strategic thinking capabilities.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
- High level of integrity, professionalism, and attention to detail.

As IT Product Owner for Supply Chain, you will lead the evolution and management of digital platforms and drive projects that enable the Avio Aero Supply Chain organization to meet the specific requirements and regulations of military programs, with a particular focus on manufacturing and quality processes.

Kulcsszerepet játszik a javított hajtómű-alkatrészek biztonságának, minőségének és megbízhatóságának biztosításában. A munkakör kémiai/vegyi vizsgálatok és elemzések elvégzését foglalja magában, amelyek célja a különböző vegyi folyamatok, oldatok, fürdők, anyagok és keverékek összetételének és tulajdonságainak értékelése, támogatva a javítási folyamatokat és a hibaelemzési vizsgálatokat. Fejlett vizsgálati technikák és berendezések alkalmazásával a technikus alapvető adatokat szolgáltat műszaki döntésekhez, és biztosítja a mindenkori ipari és belső szabványoknak, előírásoknak való megfelelést. Munkája közvetlenül hozzájárul a biztonságos, kiváló minőségű és nagy teljesítményű alkatrészek szállításához, amelyek megfelelnek a szigorú repülésbiztonsági követelményeknek. A munkakör létfontosságú a repülésbiztonság szempontjából kritikus alkatrészek integritásának és teljesítményének fenntartásában.

Job Description

Fő feladatok és felelősségek:

- Rutinszerű mérések és ellenőrzések elvégzése a vegyi gyártósorokon a meghatározott szabványoknak és előírásoknak való megfelelés érdekében. Eltérés esetén adagolási utasítások kiadása és az eredmények visszaellenőrzése.
- Ipari mosó berendezésekben használt mosó folyadékok rendszeres rutinszerű ellenőrzése. Eltérés esetén adagolási utasítások kiadása és az eredmények visszaellenőrzése.

postings.location: Lynn, Massachusetts, United States of America
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
The Lead Advanced Manufacturing Engineer (AME) plays a key role in bringing manufacturing processes to life — from process design and tooling to equipment implementation, new product introduction, and production support. This person will work closely with cross-functional teams to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost by solving shop-floor challenges, advancing manufacturing capability, and supporting production readiness for new and existing products. The ideal candidate combines strong manufacturing expertise, hands-on problem solving, and the ability to guide others in a fast-paced production environment.

In this role, you will help improve manufacturing capability, support production readiness, solve critical shop-floor challenges, and enable safe, high-quality delivery for the business. This is primarily a individual contributor role with opportunities to provide coaching, mentorship and project management through influence.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Define and control production process including tooling and equipment. Validate design specifications and shop floor application of new product, tools, or equipment. Includes Manufacturing Engineers.
- Developing in-depth knowledge of a technical discipline. Uses prior experience and acquired technical expertise to execute policy/strategy.
- Support production teams with problem solving and evolving manufacturing practices to better support customer delivery through safe and quality processes/technology.
- Source and oversee new equipment & new product introduction to production readiness.
- Support emerging technology platforms through Research & Development and Testing
- In-depth understanding of key business drivers; uses this understanding to accomplish own work. In-depth understanding of how work of own team integrates with other teams and contributes to the area.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university and a minimum of 3 years of Manufacturing & Production Process and Equipment experience (or a high school diploma/GED with a minimum of 7 years of Manufacturing & Production Process and Equipment experience)

Desired Characteristics

- Bachelor’s Degree in engineering or a related technical field from an accredited college or university and a minimum of 5 years of Manufacturing & Production Process and Equipment experience (or a high school diploma/GED with a minimum of 9 years of Manufacturing & Production Process and Equipment experience)
- Strong technical background CNC Machining and programming
- Diverse knowledge of manufacturing process and how they relate to one another
- Ability to mentor guide individuals and related technical disciplines
- Familiar with automated control type systems and logic associated with them.
- Experience in aerospace, turbine, precision machining, or other regulated manufacturing
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
- Proven ability to plan, document, and execute technical programs or projects.
- Ability to mentor others and work effectively across functions.
- Demonstrates humility, transparency, focus, and collaborative leadership.

The base pay range for this position is $116,150-155,250 USD Annual. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on October 23, 2026.
