Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants. Other benefits include tuition assistance, adoption assistance, paid parental leave, disability insurance, life insurance, and paid time-off for vacation or illness. ​

postings.location: Cheltenham, Gloucestershire, United Kingdom
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
A fantastic opportunity has arisen for a Lead Buyer to join our purchasing team in Cheltenham on a 15 month fixed term contract. In this position, you will take ownership of a group of suppliers, managing purchase order placements and address any challenges that arise. You will also escalate issues as necessary to mitigate any concerns or risks.

There is potential for this role to expand to include Long Term Agreement (LTA) and Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) placements, aligning with our commodity partnership strategy.

GE Aerospace is a world leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial, military, business, and general aviation aircraft.

Our Cheltenham facility specialises in manufacturing advanced aircraft power distribution and avionics systems. With a history dating back to 1939, the site focuses on design, development, manufacturing, and aftermarket services for major aerospace manufacturers in the civilian and military sectors.

Employees at Cheltenham have unique opportunities to work on complex projects with international clients, developing essential aircraft systems for the future.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Place and follow-up on POs. Manage relationships with suppliers for PO execution. Manage problems and schedule changes. Update ERP.
- Applies general knowledge of business developed through education or past experience. Understands how work of own team contributes to the area.
- Resolves issues using established procedures. Consults People Leader or more senior team members for issues outside of defined parameters.
- Own the 40 day requisition metric for given requisition pool - driving forecasting and management/escalation of risk
- Support the continued deployment of PFEP - improving data quality
- Partner with relevant Commodity Lead to grow buy/commodity partnership
- Maintain ownership of certain strategic suppliers

Required Qualifications

- Strong experience in Sourcing & Buying-Procurement.
- Relevant experience in Aerospace/FAR15 procurement would be an advantage

Desired Characteristics

- Strong oral and written communication skills.
- Strong interpersonal and personal leadership skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy
- Demonstrated ability to analyse and proactively resolve problems
- Proven analytical and organisational ability
- Sound commercial and financial acumen
- Strong knowledge of GE Aerospace products and services
- Knowledge of Working with Government compliance

Flexible Working

GE supports and encourages flexible working arrangements, where possible, and recognises the benefits to employees of having a positive work-life balance.

Total Reward

At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.

As a new joiner to GE we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs;

- Pension
- Bonus
- Life Assurance
- Group income protection
- Private medical cover

Security Clearance

Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS

You will work with a team of passionate and skilled engineers who share your vision of creating innovative and reliable embedded systems. To succeed in this position, you will need a background in embedded systems, a keen eye for detail, and a deep understanding of real-time systems and their constraints. You will also need to demonstrate your ability to take full ownership of your role and deliver high-quality software solutions. The role has moderate autonomy, requiring high levels of operational judgment.

- Proficiency in Ada, C, C++ or equivalent languages.
- Location: Grand Rapids, MI. This is a fully onsite position requiring attendance five days per week. A comprehensive corporate relocation package is available for eligible candidates.
- This role requires the successful candidate to maintain a US Government Security Clearance; prerequisite for a security clearance is U.S. Citizenship. Preference will be given to candidates who currently hold US Government Security Clearance.

- Extensive experience in Ada for embedded software design, development, and testing.
- Knowledge of scripting languages (Python, Perl, Tcl, etc.) and code management tools (Git, CVS, SVN, Perforce, etc.)
- Experience with network protocols with an understanding of Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking concepts, including Ethernet, Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) tagging where applicable. Familiarity with Neighbor Discovery (ND) in IPv6 is highly desirable.
- Experience implementing or integrating Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) and Internet Key Exchange (IKE) (version 1 and/or version 2).
- Experience with RTOS (Linux, FreeRTOS, QNX, VxWorks, etc.) and device drivers for complex systems using parallel processing, multi-threading, distributed processing, multi-core, SoM, and/or secure processing.

Job Description Summary
At GE Aerospace, our Field Service Engineers (FSEs) are the embodiment of our GE Aerospace behaviors- Respect for People, Continuous Improvement, and being Customer Driven. Our dedicated professionals are on the front line, working directly with our customers to solve problems and ensure the highest standards of service and support, for our customers with our customers.

Your commitment to excellence ensures that we remain a trusted partner to our customers, providing reliable and high-quality service.

Job Description

Company Overview:

Are you ready to see your career take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen.

Role Overview:

At GE Aerospace, we shape the future of flight, lift people up, and ensure they return home safely. Our Field Service Engineers embody this mission every day by being embedded within the customers site, delivering exceptional service and support. As an Airline Field Service Engineer, you will serve as the trusted on-site technical representative for our customers, with our customers. Operating independently and remotely from GE Aerospace hubs to resolve technical challenges and drive success directly in support of our customers fleets.

As part of GE Aerospace's remote Commercial Field Service organization, you will have the opportunity to travel both to support customer needs and to participate in internal conferences, fostering collaboration and continuous growth within our globally dispersed team.

More specifically, you will:

- Provide Leadership and Technical Support: Lead programs and offer technical direction and assistance to the customers in the operation, inspection, maintenance, and repair of assigned jet engine product lines.​
- Customer Advocacy: Deliver prompt, effective solutions that address customer issues and exceed their expectations, driving loyalty and long-term partnerships.
- Monitor and Improve Reliability: Track reliability and on-wing performance, including significant events, engine removals, delays, and cancellations. Influence airline stakeholders to implement critical reliability improvements.
- Enhance Maintenance Planning: Influence long-term maintenance planning to ensure the stability of the aircraft engine fleet.​
- Interpret Technical Documentation: Support maintenance and operational activities by interpreting OEM and technical manuals.

- Apply FLIGHT DECK: Utilise our FLIGHT DECK principles to deliver continuous improvement in identifying proactive reliability enhancements.
- Data Analytics and Reporting: Produce data analytics and timely reports on fleet status, program updates, events, and trends for key internal stakeholders.​
- Proactive Maintenance Recommendations: Provide recommendations for proactive maintenance based on engine performance analytics.​

The ideal candidate brings strong technical experience in airline operations, powerplant, maintenance planning, propulsion, or related engineering environments, with the ability to work independently as a trusted on-site customer representative. They are a proactive, customer-focused problem solver with strong communication, analytical, and relationship-building skills, capable of translating engine data and technical issues into practical actions that improve fleet reliability and operational performance.

- A Bachelor's of Engineering or technical degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma / GED / technical certificate with at least 4 years of full time work experience in fields noted below)
- A minimum of 4 years of full time working experience in airline operations, powerplant or maintenance planning, engineering, aviation propulsion, or other related field

- Technical expertise in aircraft engine or turbomachinery equipment.
- Experience using software or data analytics to make informed technical decisions and to provide recommendations to the customer or other key internal stakeholders.
- Self-directed with the ability to problem solve using sound judgement and critical thinking.
- Ability to lead and deliver result orientated priorities using strong project management, analytical, time management and prioritization skills.
- Strong oral and written communication skills with the ability to forge deep relations at all levels, not only with key internal stakeholders but also with the customer

At GE Aerospace, we have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen. Job Description Summary
The Lead Test Systems Engineer will own the design and delivery of automated production test systems for complex electronic aerospace products. This role combines technical leadership, hands-on development, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure safe, high-quality, and cost-effective test solutions that support manufacturing and new product introduction. This includes developing test software for full automation, managing requirements, and integrating hardware and software into complete systems.

Location: Grand Rapids, MI

This position, which offers a blend of onsite and hybrid work arrangements, is based in Grand Rapids and necessitates a presence in the office for 2-3 days each week. An extensive corporate relocation package is also available for eligible candidates.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities:

- Lead the design and development of production test equipment for complex electronic aerospace products, from concept through deployment.

- Architect and implement system-level automated test solutions, including hardware, software, and data flows, to achieve high test coverage and throughput.

- Own the full test system lifecycle: planning, requirements, architecture, hardware/software design, integration, verification, release, and sustainment.

- Influence overall test strategy and coverage, including test data analytics, design-for-test (DFT) input, and board-level test strategies in manufacturing.

- Develop and maintain test software using National Instruments TestStand, C/C++/C# in Microsoft Visual Studio, and C in LabWindows/CVI (or equivalent tools).

- Provide hands-on technical support to manufacturing, including debug of test systems, test failures, and equipment issues.

- Create and maintain test design documentation, including requirements, test specifications, schematics/drawings, procedures, test software documentation, verification procedures, and reports.

- Collaborate closely with R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, and Product Engineering to align test solutions with product requirements, safety, and quality standards.

Job Description Summary
Intergalactic, now part of Unison, a GE Aerospace Company, is a team of engineers, technologists, designers, mathematicians, and problem solvers committed to a singular idea: reviving the no-boundaries mentality in aerospace. We are a team of the nation’s best, regardless of where we live.

The Lead Engineer 1 - Thermal Dynamics provides analytical modeling capabilities to the systems engineering team by leading component and system level trade studies and working with the systems engineers to develop a system architecture to meet customer requirements. In cooperation with the Program Management team, the Lead Engineer 1 - Thermal Dynamics leads and executes thermal modeling and analysis efforts. This role is responsible for performance requirements compliance assessment, interpreting and analyzing test data, synthesizing test data and correlating system models, and building up and maintaining system models and model libraries.

During the program, the Lead Engineer 1 - Thermal Dynamics will work with a multi-disciplinary project team of subject matter experts in fields such as thermal/aerospace analysis, installation, mechanical design and analysis, reliability, controls, electronics and software, and testing.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Assisting the System Engineer with developing the program’s system architecture and technical approach. This can include thermal and controls analysis and testing and test analysis as it relates to system model correlation and performance requirements compliance assessment during development and verification and validation.
- Identify and manage program’s technical risks as it pertains to thermal performance.
- Serve as technical lead for modeling and analysis, provide clear objectives that are measurable and attainable, and coordinate modeling and analysis activities with other engineering functional groups.
- Work closely with the Systems Engineer and Program Manager to ensure successful execution of modeling, analysis, and testing development for programs.
- Manage thermal and performance technical requirements and assist the program Systems Engineer in their requirements traceability, decomposition, derivation, and verification & validation.
- Allocate and decompose high-level requirements into lower-level specifications to internal functional groups, components, and suppliers as applicable for thermal and performance requirements.
- Researching and recommending investments or changes in technology, methodology, toolsets, procedures, equipment, systems, etc. to continually improve the discipline health and the Intergalactic’s products and services.
- Communicate and collaborate with customers and suppliers as part of design development process.
- Review and approve documentation for transition from prototype to production.
- Provide engineering support to trouble shoot and diagnose non-performing products (RCCA, lessons learned, etc.).
- Perform other duties as assigned.

​​

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college and 8-10 years of relevant experience. Relevant advanced degrees, including an MS or PhD, will be considered as satisfying a portion of the industry experience requirement.

- Working knowledge of key aerospace technical disciplines including requirements management, technical verification and validation methodologies, mechanical design, materials, modeling/documentation, structural analysis, electrical systems, system controls, embedded controls, development testing and analysis, qualification analysis and testing.
- Deep expertise in the thermal fluid sciences including fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer.
- Experience and expertise in thermal fluid systems analysis and modeling including understanding of nonlinear, gradient and gradient free numerical iterative solvers and optimization techniques.

- Familiarity with environmental testing and qualification methods such as MIL-STD-810 and DO-160.
- Basic CAD experience in NX.
- Deep understanding of coding/scripting experience (preferably in MATLAB/Simulink or Python).
- Expertise building, using, correlating, and maintaining steady state and dynamic system modeling and architecting high level controls.

- Strong oral and written communication skills.

Job Description Summary

Job Description

Working at our Clearwater Location

Clearwater is a provider of engineering, circuit card assembly, OEM Avionics, and MRO services to commercial and military customers. Products and technologies here are diverse and highly sophisticated. Your work will contribute to systems that manage the performance of Boeing 737 and 787 aircraft as well as F-18s, F-35s, Harriers, and Apaches. Not only will you work in a facility that has been awarded OSHAS’s highest safety rating, but you’ll be part of a diverse team of employees working together to impact the future of flight for generations.

Role Overview

The Lead Manufacturing Engineer (1st Shift) will be responsible for the development and implementation of manufacturing processes, ensuring they meet our stringent safety, quality, delivery, and cost objectives. This role requires a strong background in manufacturing engineering, project management, and a deep understanding of Lean manufacturing principles.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Utilize your experience or expertise to solve problems, develop and execute objectives for self and others, and have the ability to effect short-term and some long-term business goals
- Develop and maintain manufacturing work instructions and related documentation
- Design and build / procure necessary fixtures and tooling to manufacture electronic assemblies and products
- Support assembly equipment upgrades from purchase through installation
- Conduct cost / benefit analysis for changes to manufacturing processes and / or equipment
- Assist Production Supervisors and production employees in resolving manufacturing process problems through a drive to root cause and permanent corrective action
- Support EHS projects in cell
- Drive Process Improvement / Cycle Reduction initiatives and drive productivity improvements via process changes or improvements
- Support the quality function through integration of ISO / QC documentation and manufacturing work instructions
- Lead high impact process and quality improvement projects yielding significant reduction in defects and increased productivity in the Cell
- Attend weekly cross-functional quality sessions and track/drive root cause analysis and corrective actions for Cell issues
- Lead New Technology Initiatives (NTI) and share best practices with other locations
- Utilize lean-manufacturing principles and participate in action workouts to improve process capability, reduce overall costs and increase capacity defects and increased productivity in the Cell

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university (or a High School diploma / GED with at least 7 years of experience in Manufacturing / Production)
- Minimum of 3 years of experience in electronics assembly environments
- This position requires U.S. citizenship status

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in running, supporting, troubleshooting, fixing, and resolving line issues with some of the following Circuit Card Assembly Cells: SMT Prep, Mag-Load, Fuji SMT, SPI, Reflow Ovens, Through Hole, Hand Assembly, Selective Solder, Wave Solder, Bonding, Conformal Coating, DePanel, Final Assembly, and Box load

- Ability to read engineering drawings and specifications
- Strong mechanical design ability
- Ability to manage priorities and achieve results
- Prior exposure to and knowledge of Lean Manufacturing

- Strong manufacturing process knowledge

- Strong interpersonal and leadership skills

postings.description:
Job Description Summary
The Lead Manufacturing Engineer – NPI is responsible for the timely development and industrialization of Component Repair New Product Introduction (NPI) projects, working with relevant functional teams, and ensuring safety, quality, delivery and cost objectives are met.

Job Description

Company Overview:

Are you ready to see your career take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen.

Site Overview:

For more than 40 years, our advanced facilities in Singapore have led aerospace innovation across Asia Pacific. From automating processes to leveraging smart factory technologies, robotics, and additive manufacturing, GE Aerospace is shaping the future of aviation at GE Aerospace Engine Services Singapore (GEAESS).

GEAESS is our largest site for engine component Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO), responsible for more than 60% of our global repair volume.

Role Overview:

- Lead the development of repair processes for Component Repair New Product Introduction (NPI).

- Generate manufacturing routers and instructions, Repair Source Substantiation packages, and other documentation required for industrialization and approval.

- Lead resolution of technical and operational challenges or concerns raised, and ensure follow through till approval is obtained and repair is handed over to shop operations.

- Work closely with the Repair, Design and Product Support Engineering teams in Singapore, USA & other global sites, during the NPI repair development phase & industrialization.

- Manage multiple NPI projects by providing scheduling, resource management, budget control and EHS compliance.

- Lead and effectively interface with Operations, Quality, Engineering, and other support teams during NPI repair industrialization in the Shop, and ensure that it meets Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost objectives, within schedule and budget.

- Interface with vendors and internal functions in an effective manner to ensure that the action items to be carried out for the NPI are executed on time and on budget.

- Assure that all engineering designs and technical data are completed and accurately documented to provide an accurate technical/historical base for future reference and to meet customer / end user requirements.

- Participate in Lean initiatives, including continuous improvement of repair processes, and utilize FLIGHT DECK tools for NPI process improvements.

- Implement new technology and/or process improvements to increase productivity of new repair processes.

Ideal Candidate

- The ideal candidate should have a good grasp of key repair manufacturing processes, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and collaborate effectively across global teams to deliver on performance objectives.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in Mechanical / Aerospace / Materials or other relevant Engineering discipline with 3-5 years of experience in NPI.

Preferred Qualifications

- Good understanding of manufacturing and inspection tools and processes used in the repair industry – brazing, heat treat, diffusion coating/thermal spray, peening, welding/additive, machining, etc.

- Working knowledge of blueprints, application of engine manuals and technical substantiation process will be an advantage.

- Knowledge of GD&T, tool/fixture design and applications in repair.

- Good time management and strong organizational skills, with ability to multi-task to meet deadlines and customer needs.

- Knowledge of Lean principles, tools and methodology.

- Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn

- Transparent: shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively

- Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed

- Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative

- Problem solver: analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker.

At GE Aerospace, we have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen. Here, you will have the opportunity to work on really cool things with really smart and collaborative people. Together, we will mobilize a new era of growth in aerospace and defense. Where others stop, we accelerate.

The Lead Manufacturing Engineer – Coatings Manufacturing Readiness supports the design, sourcing, and production of complex aerospace components and assemblies for Edison Works Advanced Programs. In this role, you will drive design for manufacturing readiness, producibility, reduce manufacturing cost and risk, and ensure our suppliers along with internal GE shops can deliver safely, on quality, on time, and at cost — with a specific focus on coatings and surface engineering technologies.The job allows modification of procedures and practices covering work as long as the end results meet standards of acceptability (quality, volume, timeliness etc.).

Roles and Responsibilities

- Leverages expertise in one or more coatings and surface engineering areas, such as thermal spray (HVOF, plasma, cold spray), electron beam physical vapor deposition (EB-PVD), diffusion/aluminide coatings, slurry and sol-gel coatings, thermal barrier coatings (TBCs), environmental barrier coatings (EBCs), plating, and other surface treatments.

- Manages integrated schedules, aligns cross-functional teams, and ensures on-time, at-cost execution of commitments.
- Acts as a key interface with DoD customers, managing contractual obligations and fostering clear communication across stakeholders.

- Adopts FLIGHT DECK actively in all aspects of work scopes, using Standard Work, Action Planning, and Problem Solving effectively. Uses technical experience, expertise, and data analysis to support recommendations.

The Lead Manufacturing Engineer – Fabrication Manufacturing Readiness supports the design, sourcing, and production of complex aerospace components and assemblies for Edison Works Advanced Programs. In this role, you will drive design for manufacturing readiness, producibility, reduce manufacturing cost and risk, and ensure our suppliers along with internal GE shops can deliver safely, on quality, on time, and at cost — with a specific focus on fabrication technologies.

Job Description

* Drive manufacturing readiness for complex fabrication processes (e.g., machining, forming, welding, additive manufacturing) from concept through production launch.
* Collaborate with design engineering, supply chain, and quality teams to ensure design for manufacturability (DFM) and assembly (DFA).

Job Description

Working at our Clearwater Location

Clearwater is a provider of engineering, circuit card assembly, OEM Avionics, and MRO services to commercial and military customers. Your work will contribute to systems that manage the performance of Boeing 737 and 787 aircraft as well as F-18s, F-35s, Harriers, and Apaches. The Lead Manufacturing Quality Engineer works with a team of Quality Engineers to ensure the highest standards of product quality, compliance, and continuous improvement across the manufacturing lifecycle. - Collaborate with other Manufacturing Quality Engineers, providing guidance, training, and feedback as needed.

- Act as a primary contact for customer quality concerns and interface with regulatory bodies during audits.

This role helps standardize readiness execution and sustain momentum through disciplined follow-up, visual management, and action-oriented problem solving. postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Teams in the Next Generation Products space are energized with a passion for the aerospace industry and are devoted to supporting our military customers. We develop breakthrough technologies to create the future of military propulsion, continuing GE's long history of engineering excellence.

As a premier NPI, NGP1 is fast paced and setting new standards for Edison Works. The Program Mechanical Design team is a large organization with multiple sub-teams. This role is aligned to a sub-team spanning multiple commodities and design phases, including cost-out design, hardware delivery, test, certification/qualification, and technical publications. This role operates in a highly cross-functional environment, enabling rapid learning and product maturation, and will help lead the charge on FLIGHT DECK adoption within Edison Works, applying lean principles to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost across the NPI lifecycle.

The NGP Lead Design Engineer owns the design, development, and qualification of advanced military products, specifically hot structural components. The engineer is responsible for planning/executing technical design tasks including analysis and manufacturing support of assigned hardware in addition to program management of hardware cost, weight, and schedule deliverables. The role has some autonomy but is focused on execution of activities within an operating discipline covered by standard functional practices and procedures. Some judgment may be required but this is typically with guidance. This position reports to an engineering manager in Evendale, OH with the opportunity to integrate with various internal and external engineering disciplines.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Execute the design, analysis, and evaluation of assigned components for advanced military products

- Adhere to business standards, practices, procedures, and product requirements

- Leverage prior mechanical design experience and broaden knowledge of one's own technical discipline to meet product deliverables within schedule and budget constraints

- Demonstrate systems-thinking mentality to understand how work of one's team integrates with others to achieve product requirements

- Exhibit autonomy to make decisions within a defined requirements framework while resolving design challenges in situations which require technical knowledge and judgment

- Review designs and consult with senior technical leaders for evaluation of work

- This role requires sound interpersonal skills to develop strong internal and external customer relationships by serving as an interface point within GE

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s or advanced degree in engineering from an accredited university
- Minimum of 3 years' experience in a mechanical design, mechanical analysis or similar engineering position
- This role requires the successful candidate to maintain a US Government Security Clearance; prerequisite for a security clearance is U.S. Citizenship. Preference will be given to candidates who currently hold US Government Security Clearance.
- Ability to travel up to 10% of the time.

Desired Characteristics

- Bachelor's or advanced degree in mechanical, aerospace or similar engineering from an accredited university
- Possess an existing US Government Security Clearance
- Highly motivated, passionate about the NGP mission, and with strong communication skills
- Demonstrated ability to analyze and solve technical challenges with sound reasoning, project planning, execution, and documentation
- Strong oral and written communication skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems. Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs. Established project management skills.
- Team-oriented, growth-driven, and people-savvy: Demonstrates humility and a team-first mindset, shows strong drive and ownership to continuously improve outcomes, and brings high interpersonal awareness to communicate effectively, build trust, and collaborate across diverse stakeholders.
- Experience with finite element analysis software such as ANSYS and 3D modelling software such as NX Unigraphics
- Experience with structural component design and analysis

postings.location: Loves Park, Illinois, United States of America
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
GE Aerospace is seeking a Lead Mechanical Test Engineer to join our team in Loves Park, Illinois. In this full-time, onsite role, you will help design and develop high-reliability aerospace products that support critical aircraft systems. Working as part of an Integrated Product Team, you will lead engineering efforts across the full product lifecycle, including bid and proposal support, technology maturation, new product introduction, production, and test.

This position focuses on advanced aerospace electromechanical and pneumatic products, including bleed air valves and linear actuators. The ideal candidate brings strong technical depth, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to lead design, analysis, testing, and cross-functional problem-solving efforts in a collaborative environment.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Lead the design, analysis, development, and testing of aerospace electromechanical and pneumatic products, including bleed air valves and linear actuators.
- Execute engineering work in accordance with sound engineering principles, program requirements, and business standards, practices, and procedures.
- Support products and programs across multiple phases, including bid and proposal, technology maturation, new product introduction, production, and test.
- Drive technical execution for assigned projects, including design reviews, risk reduction activities, and validation efforts.
- Provide technical leadership in new product development and technology maturation initiatives.
- Guide and support other technical team members while contributing as a key member of an Integrated Product Team.
- Apply analytical thinking and engineering expertise to solve product and system-level problems.
- Work cross-functionally with internal teams to ensure designs meet performance, quality, cost, and schedule objectives.
- Recommend and develop solutions outside of established parameters when needed, using sound judgment and prior experience.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a minimum of 2 years of professional experience; OR Associate degree with a minimum of 4 years of professional experience; OR High school diploma / GED with a minimum of 6 years of professional experience

Desired Qualifications

- Experience in the design, analysis, or support of electromechanical and/or pneumatic systems
- Experience leading projects or providing technical direction to engineering team members
- Experience with electromechanical actuators, pneumatic valves, or similar aerospace/mechanical systems
- Demonstrated experience with electric motors, RVDTs, resolvers, and related electrical components
- Proficiency in CAD tools, preferably SolidWorks and/or NX
- Proficiency in LabView programming and utilizing LabView for test data
- Familiarity with DO-160 testing, FAR 25/FAR 33 certification, and aerospace development processes
- Knowledge of AS9100 quality standards
- Familiarity with Lean principles and methodologies
- Strong problem-solving, analytical, and project management skills
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively across teams
- Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and able to work independently in a fast-paced engineering environment

The base pay range for this position is $95,000 – $127,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. postings.title: Lead Powerplant Engineer
postings.location: Subang, Selangor, Malaysia
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Leads the Powerplant Engineering function that interfaces with other functions to provide coordination of workscoping effectiveness, meeting customer needs on respective engines and responsible for the team's SQDIP metrics using Flightdeck. Functions with some autonomy but guided by established policies or review of end results. The job allows modification of procedures and practices covering work as long as the end results meet standards of acceptability (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost through Flightdeck).

Job Description

Company Overview:

Working at GE Aerospace means you are bringing your unique perspective, innovative spirit, drive, and curiosity to a collaborative and diverse team working to advance aerospace for future generations. If you have ideas, we will listen. Join us and see your ideas take flight!

Site Overview:

GE Aerospace Engine Services Malaysia (GEESM) in Subang plays a vital role in ensuring the safety and performance of aviation fleets every day. Established in 1997 as a Center of Excellence for CFM56 engines, GEESM has grown into a key hub of our global operations. It now services commercial aircraft engines, components, and accessories.

Employing more than 700 highly skilled local professionals and providing MRO services to more than 50 airlines worldwide, GEESM continues to exceed our customers’ expectations. With our technical expertise and pioneering spirit, we elevate the flying experience to new heights.

Role Overview:

- Directly involved in Powerplant Engineer's manpower planning that supports production team on engine workscoping.

- Managing engine workscopes for shop induction pipeline.

- Driving SQDIP metrics for Powerplant Engineering Team by utilizing fully the Flightdeck principles.

- Driving cost saving initiatives by either Challenging engine workscope status quo or researching engine part/component historical data via CFMi salesforce or MRB review board.

- Lead/manage engine investigations to determine root causes of engine issues that supports fleet management.

- Involved in Safety Action Group initiatives that drives SMS implementation and adherence in shop.

Ideal Candidate:

- Candidate will have a strong background in powerplant engineering, including expertise in engine/propulsion systems, thermodynamics, and basic engine system operation along with a focus on safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The ideal candidate should hold a technical degree in aerospace, mechanical, or related engineering fields, with at least 5 years of experience in powerplant & engine workscoping. Demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and manage complex projects is essential.

Required Qualifications:

- Degree in Aviation, Mechanical or relevant engineering field.

- Minimum 5 years of related experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Ability to manage KPIs that drives team performance in meeting set goals, ensuring team accountability and foster a transformational mindset for measurable improvement against set Team KPIs.

- Strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative, lead by example, Strong interpersonal, leadership and team-building skills.

- Analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker, pro-active

- Quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed

- Respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn

- Shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively

Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

postings.location: Vandalia, Ohio, United States of America
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You will be part of a team that embraces your drive, curiosity, and unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you will share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world.

Job Description

About the Role

As a Lead Production Quality Specialist, you will play a critical role in ensuring product quality throughout the manufacturing process. Based in Vandalia, OH, you will support quality assurance and quality control activities that enable the delivery of safe, reliable, and compliant aerospace products.

This role has meaningful autonomy within established functional practices and procedures. You will use your technical knowledge, prior experience, and sound judgment to resolve manufacturing quality issues, improve processes, and partner across teams to support operational performance.

In this role you will:

- Own quality assurance and quality control activities associated with manufacturing processes, products, and services.
- Ensure conformance through manufacturing process reviews, incoming goods control, product inspection, and witness-point activities.
- Apply technical expertise and knowledge of manufacturing quality practices to execute quality policies, strategies, and procedures.
- Analyze straightforward quality and production issues, identify root causes, and recommend solutions with guidance as needed.
- Partner with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, and other internal stakeholders to resolve issues and support departmental objectives.
- Use knowledge of business and operational drivers to prioritize work and understand the impact of quality activities across the broader organization.
- Interpret internal and external business challenges and recommend best practices to improve products, processes, and services.
- Stay informed of relevant industry trends and apply insights that support the broader quality function.
- Provide informal guidance, coaching, and support to new team members.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a detail-oriented quality professional with experience supporting manufacturing operations and improving process performance. You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, communicate clearly across functions, and take ownership of delivering high-quality results.

You are comfortable working within established processes while using judgment to identify practical improvements. You have a continuous-improvement mindset and can translate quality requirements into disciplined execution on the production floor.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college OR a high school diploma/GED with at least 6 years of experience in a relevant job family group or function.
- Experience in manufacturing and production quality, including quality assurance and/or quality control activities.
- Ability to apply technical and analytical thinking to resolve manufacturing quality issues.
- Ability to work effectively within established quality systems, policies, and procedures.

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong oral and written communication skills.
- Have QMS and APQP Knowledge.
- Demonstrated ability to analyze problems, identify solutions, and drive issue resolution.
- Experience with product inspection, incoming goods control, manufacturing conformance, and process quality.
- Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs or improvement initiatives.
- Established project management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and a continuous-improvement mindset.
- Proven interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.

The International Trade Compliance (ITC) team ensures the rigorous and compliant execution of global export controls, sanctions laws, and related regulations. The successful candidate will serve as a key contributor within the ITC team and partner closely with GE Aerospace programs and functions to apply international trade laws and regulations in support of the company’s expanding global business operations.

Job Description

Roles & Responsibilities

Consistent with the mission of the ITC team, the primary responsibilities of the Lead Specialist – ITC include, but are not limited to:

- Oversee export shipment operations by ensuring strict compliance with applicable authorizations, accurately decrementing licenses, and coordinating across departments to proactively resolve shipment-related issues.
- Prepare, review, and file export declarations with precision, ensuring full accuracy and regulatory compliance.
- Conduct systematic audits of export declaration records to verify proper filings, identify discrepancies, and maintain data integrity.
- Monitor, track, and report on trade compliance activities, including license decrementation metrics, status updates, and key performance indicators.

- Identify opportunities for and drive process and procedure improvements, coordinating cross-functional implementation efforts to enhance operational efficiency.
- Collaborate on projects and initiatives of varying scope and complexity as a valued member of cross-functional teams.

These responsibilities are performed with a degree of autonomy, with guidance and oversight from senior ITC professionals provided as appropriate based on the employee’s experience and demonstrated competencies.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience, with a minimum of 4 years of progressive, relevant experience in trade compliance or a closely related field.
- Demonstrated experience in export operations, including end-to-end process management and ensuring regulatory compliance in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience with DDTC and BIS licensing applications.
- Strong working knowledge and practical application of International Trade Compliance regulations—including ITAR, EAR, and U.S. Customs requirements—particularly in high-volume, operationally intensive settings.

- Proficiency with DECCS and SNAP-R platforms
- Unwavering commitment to compliance, ethics, and integrity

Job Description Summary
Help define the future of flight at GE Aerospace. As a Lead Systems Engineer - Avionics Networking, you will play a key role in developing advanced networked avionics solutions that enable safe, reliable, and deterministic communication across next-generation aerospace platforms.

In this role, you will lead systems engineering efforts for the Networking product line, working across software, hardware, test, safety, reliability, and certification teams to deliver high-integrity products from concept through verification and certification. You will help shape system architecture, define and manage requirements, drive integration and validation, and support certification for highly complex airborne networking systems.

postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Are you ready to see your career take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, electronics, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen.

The Lead Testing Engineer will lead the design, development, and integration of test software and hardware that enables testing of aviation power equipment in both R&D and production environments. In this role, you will partner closely with product design and manufacturing teams to ensure our products are highly testable, reliable, and ready to transition efficiently from development into manufacturing.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys software and electrical design, test system development, and cross-functional collaboration in a fast-paced aerospace environment.

At GE Aerospace in Dayton, OH the EPISCenter is the headquarters for our Electric Power and Propulsion business. At this facility you have an opportunity to put your engineering training and skills to use. Our engineers are focused and challenged on developing new technologies and delivering state of the art products such as hybrid electric power systems, the latest military power platforms, and highly efficient legacy / commercial AC power systems as seen on the F-18 and the new Boeing 777X. Plus, if you like hands-on work, there is also a 155,000 sq ft lab that includes 7 high power test cells totaling 15 MW, an EMI chamber, an electronics lab, a rapid build prototype lab, and a real time simulator lab with all the latest equipment.

The Advanced Technology Organization is responsible for driving growth through technology by researching customer needs both met and unmet, then finding solutions. Our team supports both military and commercial customers in land, sea, and air domains.

Design and develop test software and hardware

- Develop and enhance modular, reusable test architectures for manufacturing and engineering design and build verification.
- Develop test software for interfacing with large amounts of equipment and electrical signals using NI LabVIEW and TestStand.
- Design test equipment components, fixtures, and adapters using AutoCAD Electrical, Altium, and/or Siemens NX.

- Define and implement project plans, manage milestones, and conduct design and readiness reviews to ensure reliable test systems are delivered on time.
- Manage project deliverables to meet schedule, quality, and performance requirements.

- Complete the formal release process for test equipment design documents
- Write test equipment design / verification plans, equipment operation procedures, and test reports aligned to product requirements.
- Investigate test failures, perform root-cause analysis, and communicate and execute corrective actions with stakeholders.

- Work with test equipment including thermal chambers, oil carts, chillers, data acquisition systems, cDAQ / PXI systems, pressure controllers, DMMs, oscilloscopes, and related lab equipment.
- Apply knowledge of physical sensors (voltage, current, pressure, acceleration, flow, temperature) in fixture and test setup design.
- Support and/or lead efforts to automate processes and testing to improve manufacturing yields and reduce production time.
- Support the transition of products from development to manufacturing through robust test solutions.

Job Description Summary
The Greenville Machine Operator is a skilled role that involves the manufacturing of complex engine components, working with exotic aerospace alloys on some of the latest CNC machine tools in a clean, air-conditioned facility. Successful candidates will participate in a self-directed team environment to identify and implement process improvement opportunities resulting in improved quality and product flow.

Job Description

Company Intro/About Us:

Are you ready to elevate your future? You’ll be warmly welcomed at GE Aerospace where we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. You’ll learn and achieve as part of an on-going LEAN transformation. And, most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world.

Greenville Site Overview:

Working at our Greenville Facility: Advanced technology, advanced thinking and a superb work environment. When you come to work at the GE Aerospace Airfoils facility in Greenville, you’ll come to realize that you’re in a place where you can do your best. We’re producing High Pressure Turbine Blades that help power tomorrow’s commercial and military aircraft. We’re using innovative production methodologies including complex machining, special processes, and NDT.

Role Overview:

The Greenville Machine Operator is a skilled role that involves the manufacturing of complex engine components, working with exotic aerospace alloys on some of the latest CNC machine tools in a clean, air-conditioned facility. Successful candidates will participate in a self-directed team environment to identify and implement process improvement opportunities resulting in improved quality and product flow.

- Perform set-ups, tool changes, offsets, and run production on various CNC and non-CNC machines
- Identify and implement process improvement opportunities to include reduction of setup times and improvements in quality and throughput utilizing Lean Manufacturing techniques
- Must perform precision work to exacting tolerances
- Read and understand process operation sheets, tooling sheets, tech plans and associated documents
- Work from blue prints and work instructions to produce parts
- Have the ability to correctly gauge parts and record dimensions

The Ideal Candidate:

An Ideal candidate for our Machine Operator role would typically posses technical skills, Experience, and Attention to Detail. Problem Solving and Safety awareness would be beneficial on the job as well. These characteristics combined would make someone an ideal candidate for this role.

Required Qualifications:

- High School diploma or GED
- A minimum of 1 year of full time manufacturing experience with manual or Computer Numerical Controlled machining using milling, turning, lasering and grinding processes or
- An associate’s degree or higher in a manufacturing or engineering discipline (for example, Computer Integrated Machining or Engineering Technology) including graduation from any recognized machinist or toolmaker apprenticeship or certification program
- Must be willing to work Weekend Shift
- Must successfully complete pre-employment physical/drug screen and on-going random drug screens

Preferred Qualifications:

- The ability to work from layouts and dimensions on drawings and read manual gauges
- The ability to load, align, and set up machine per drawing instructions and maintain quality production records
- The ability to read blueprints and be able to read shop math and have proficient knowledge of machining methods and cutting tools
- Strong computer skills are preferred
- Must be able to wear personal protective equipment (safety glasses, gloves, hats, and safety shoes)

You’ll work in a highly technical environment where quality and safety matter every day.

This is a great opportunity for a machinist who wants to do more than just load parts - someone who can own setups, understand the process, make smart adjustments, and help drive performance on the floor.

Job Description

What you’ll do:

As a CNC Machinist, you’ll be a hands-on technical resource responsible for producing aerospace hardware to print and process requirements. Responsibilities include:

CNC Setup and Machining

- Perform independent setups on CNC lathes, turning centers, and grinding equipment, including work holding, tooling, offsets, and first-piece validation

- Operate CNC and grinding equipment, monitor process performance, and make approved adjustments to maintain quality and dimensional control

- Verify wheel/tool selection, dress grinding wheels, and monitor tool wear, wheel wear, part growth, and other conditions affecting process capability

Blueprint Reading, Process Control, and Inspection

- Read and interpret engineering drawings, routers, specifications, GD&T, and inspection requirements

- Understand and machine to dimensional requirements such as runout, concentricity, profile, surface finish, and tight tolerances

- Make minor G-code edits as authorized and perform in-process/final inspection using precision measuring tools

- Document inspection results and validate first-piece acceptance to requirements

Troubleshooting and Problem Solving

- Identify and address machining issues such as chatter, taper, lobing, burn, size drift, and runout

- Stop work and escalate nonconformances when required

- Support containment, corrective actions, and collaboration with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to improve process stability and performance

Documentation, Traceability, and Continuous Improvement

- Complete production, quality, and system documentation accurately while maintaining part traceability and lot control

- Support first article inspection, documentation and required work order transactions

- Participate in kaizen and continuous improvement efforts to reduce scrap, rework, and cycle time

- Support standard work, 5S, continuous improvement, and routine operator maintenance including cleaning and coolant checks

What we’re looking for:

Required qualifications

- High school diploma, GED, or vocational school certificate

- Minimum 5 years of machining experience in a manufacturing environment

- Experience with CNC turning and/or grinding, including the ability to perform independent machine setups

- Proven ability to machine parts to tight tolerances with experience using precision measurement tools and recording inspection results to specification

- Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and GD&T

- This role may encounter high risk or hazardous operations and/or include working shifts beyond a standard workweek. As such, a requirement of the role is to be at least 18 years of age by the time of joining

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in aerospace manufacturing

- Experience working in controlled manufacturing environments with strict documentation and traceability requirements

- Experience machining precision aerospace components

- Experience with First Article Inspection (FAI), including AS9102

- Experience machining advanced materials such as ceramic composites

- Experience with 3-axis and 5-axis vertical and horizontal machining centers

- Experience with multi-axis turning centers and complex workholding

- Strong troubleshooting skills and a proactive approach to process improvement

At GE Aerospace, we invent the future of flight, lift people up, and bring them home safely. For the people of GE Aerospace, their work isn't just a job. It's their passion and purpose. Job Summary:

The Manufacturing Engineering Development Program (MEDP) is a 2-year development program in manufacturing focused on developing and accelerating technical expertise across the Supply Chain. Engineers in the MEDP will work in manufacturing engineering assignments to gain experience through a mix of on-the-job training and classroom education structured to provide a foundation of technical and leadership skills. You'll complete two 12-month assignments to cultivate growth in key technical disciplines and engineering responsibilities. In addition, the MEDP will foster mentorship and structured learning opportunities with our team of manufacturing experts. Upon completion, you will be ready for promotional opportunities to further advance in GE Aerospace.

- Provide daily hands-on support to shop floor personnel to help facilitate problem-solving and process improvements related to production or development labs.

- Apply geometric dimensioning and tolerancing skills and interpret blueprints to facilitate component manufacturing processes.

- Utilize various design and analytical software to support and improve manufacturing processes.

- Advance and develop manufacturing planning, processes and work instructions.

- Work with cross-functional teams to identify and implement process improvements to improve product quality, increase throughput, and reduce manufacturing costs.

- Collect and analyze data from manufacturing processes to drive short- and long-term actions that support production.

- Apply Lean and Six Sigma tools to identify waste and support decision-making processes.

- Manage project plans related to manufacturing changes and collaborate with various functions to drive action and project closure.

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering or a related field from an accredited university or college (or an associate degree in Engineering or a Technology discipline with at least 3 years of manufacturing experience)

- Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn

postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Unison, a GE Aerospace company, is the leading provider of differentiated engine controls, accessories, and performance monitoring solutions in the Aerospace, Defense & Space segments. Serving both original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket customers, Unison designs, manufactures and supplies the most advanced components and systems in the world.

We are now seeking a 1st Shift Production Supervisor to join our amazing team in Dayton, OH. This will be a challenging coach role that will perform the daily operations of the plant to ensure reliability and consistency on the production line. Impacts departmental operations and responsible for planning/execution. The role has some autonomy but is focused on execution of activities within an operating discipline covered by standard functional practices and procedures. Some judgment may be required but this is typically with guidance.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Oversight and management of front-line manufacturing employees. Typically managing hourly employee populations.
- Developing in-depth knowledge of a technical discipline.
- Uses prior experience and acquired technical expertise to execute policy/strategy.
- In-depth understanding of key business drivers; uses this understanding to accomplish own work.
- In-depth understanding of how work of own team integrates with other teams and contributes to the area.
- Uses some level of judgment and has ability to propose different solutions outside of set parameters but with guidance.
- Uses prior experience and on-the-job training to solve straightforward tasks.
- Has access to technical skills and analytic thinking required to solve problems.
- May use multiple internal sources outside of own team to arrive at decisions.
- A job at this level is likely to be an individual contributor with proven interpersonal skills or an early people leader who can hire and develop talent.
- Provides informal guidance to new team members
- Leads through FLIGHT DECK principles

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university plus a minimum of 3 years of experience Manufacturing & Production Supervision, OR; A High School Diploma / GED with a minimum of 7 years of experience Manufacturing & Production Supervision

Desired Characteristics

- Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn
- Transparent: shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively
- Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed
- Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative
- Problem solver: analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker

Company Intro/About GE Aerospace

GE Aerospace is a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. The Marine Customer Account Manager is accountable for helping deliver Marine Spares business performance and customer readiness outcomes by ensuring spare parts are quoted, ordered, and shipped without delay. Job Description Summary
We are seeking a motivated Metrology Technician to join our turbine airfoils machining NPI team at the BladeworX facility. Reporting to the Site Quality Leader and taking day-to-day technical direction from our Senior Metrologist, you will learn to operate and program our inspection equipment and grow into an increasingly independent contributor. This is a hands-on, development-oriented role for someone eager to build deep technical expertise in dimensional inspection and measurement science within a fast-paced New Product Introduction environment.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

- Learn to operate, program, and maintain a range of inspection equipment (e.g., CMMs, vision systems, and other dimensional measurement tools) under the guidance of the Senior Metrologist.
- Assist with, and progressively take ownership of, weekly inspection equipment calibrations to ensure measurement accuracy and traceability.
- Support the creation and revision of inspection programs for new and existing turbine airfoil parts.
- Participate in troubleshooting and problem-solving of inspection equipment issues, measurement discrepancies, and hardware inspection non-conformances.
- Document inspection results, calibration records, and program changes in accordance with quality standards and procedures.
- Collaborate with machining, engineering, and quality teams to support NPI part qualification and continuous improvement efforts.

Minimum Required Qualifications:

- Associate’s degree or a high school diploma/GED from an accredited school or institution

- Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn​

- Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed ​

- Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative​

- Problem solver: analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker

- Familiarity with CMM operations or programming a plus (training provided).
- Basic computer proficiency and comfort learning new software.
- Ability to work 1st shift (6:30 am – 2:30 pm) in a manufacturing/lab environment.

Because this role is intended to develop over time, we are especially interested in candidates who demonstrate:

- Curiosity and a growth mindset — a genuine desire to learn the "why" behind measurement methods, not just the "how."
- Strong problem-solving instincts — the ability to methodically break down inspection issues and non-conformances and work toward root cause.
- Attention to detail and precision — a natural rigor with data, tolerances, and documentation.

Job Description

For more than 22 years, our manufacturing facilities in Wilmington have been the driving force behind the growth and success of GE Aerospace. With 600,000 square feet of manufacturing space and an advanced mix of over 300 CNC machines and 21 special processes, we produce high-quality rotating parts for commercial and military aircraft engines. Our team plays a crucial role in introducing advanced new technologies like the LEAP and 9x Engines, offering outstanding opportunities to contribute to the future of aviation.

As a CNC Machine Operator, you will play a crucial role in setting up and operating multi-axis CNC/NC machines, often running multiple machines simultaneously. Your work will involve handling a variety of metals and parts with close tolerances and fine finishes. Utilizing complex measuring devices such as micrometers, calipers, indicators, and special purpose gages, you will generate and check part dimensions during various machining stages with precision. Your expertise in precise indicating on parts, where true indicator reading (TIR) and four-point indication are critical, will ensure the highest quality standards are met.

You could be a strong military fit for this role if you have formal machinist or metalworking training (DoD machinist school, vocational machinist program, or similar), experience reading and interpreting mechanical drawings/blueprints, tolerances, and finishes, and regularly use precision measuring tools.

Key Responsibilities:

- Dimensional Accuracy: Utilize complex measuring devices to generate and check part dimensions during various machining stages, ensuring precision and accuracy

- Critical Indication: Perform precise indicating on parts, where true indicator reading (TIR) and four-point indication are essential to the machining process

- Record Keeping: Accurately account for your time using the prescribed system, electronically maintain records, logbooks, and charts, and produce electronic or manual reports

- Training and Development: Help train operators to use specific equipment, sharing your expertise and fostering a collaborative learning environment

- Quality Assurance: Achieve all required tolerances and finishes that meet standards set by Manufacturing Engineering and Quality Assurance, ensuring all characteristics generated at designated operations are conforming through applicable inspection techniques

- Certification: Obtain and maintain the CVP certification, with training provided to support your professional growth

- Traceability: Accurately serialize parts to maintain traceability at all times, ensuring compliance with industry standards

- Team Collaboration: Actively participate in daily team meetings and activities, practicing direct professional communication with team members and contributing to a positive team dynamic

- Equipment Operation: Perform set-up and operation of equipment according to drawings, method sheets, and occasionally supplement this information with your own job knowledge

- Material Handling: Utilize forklifts, cranes, and material handling equipment to lift or carry objects weighing up to 50 lbs, following proper ergonomic procedures

Required Qualifications

- Active Military personnel on their last 180 days of Military service
- High School Diploma or equivalent
- Expertise in CNC Machining: Bring your extensive manufacturing or military experience, with at least 3 years in the setup and operation of CNC machining processes such as drilling, milling, grinding, turning, or broaching, or leverage your 2-year degree from an accredited machinist training program to excel in this role
- Proficiency in Technical Interpretation and Precision Measurement: Utilize your skills in reading and interpreting mechanical blueprints and production planning, along with at least 2 years of experience using precision measuring instruments, to ensure the highest standards of quality and accuracy in every task

Job Description

This role supports Marine and Industrial engine programs, including LM2500, LM6000, LMS100, and legacy programs such as CF6 and F110, with a focus on enabling safe, compliant, and timely engine shipment. The position requires blueprint interpretation, dimensional inspection, and strong cross-functional execution with engineering, planning, and operations teams to resolve issues and maintain product flow. This role is expected to uphold Safety first, followed by Quality, Delivery, and Productivity, while supporting accurate documentation and continuous improvement within the quality system.

This role is structured for high performers to be developed into Quality Engineer roles

Roles and Responsibilities

- Review engineering drawings, specifications, and technical documentation to determine First Article Inspection requirements and product acceptance criteria.
- Interpret blueprints and perform dimensional inspection activities to verify hardware conformance to design intent and manufacturing requirements.
- Develop, maintain, and execute First Article Inspection plans in accordance with applicable business processes, quality requirements, and customer expectations.
- Perform First Article Inspection activities for components and assemblies supporting Marine and Industrial engine programs.
- Compile, validate, and upload First Article Inspection documentation and records into ECAV in a complete, accurate, and timely manner.
- Partner with engineering to resolve drawing issues, clarify technical requirements, and address product or documentation discrepancies.
- Work closely with planning, operations, and other cross-functional teams to support execution priorities and help ensure engines are shipped in compliance with the quality system.
- Support product quality and inspection readiness across LM2500, LM6000, LMS100, CF6, and F110 programs.
- Identify risks, gaps, and improvement opportunities that may affect Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Productivity.
- Maintain accurate inspection records and support compliance with internal procedures, customer requirements, and regulatory standards as applicable.
- Contribute to continuous improvement efforts that strengthen inspection effectiveness, process discipline, and overall business performance.

Required Qualifications

- Active Military personnel on their last 180 days of Military service
- Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university or a high school diploma / GED with a minimum of 4 years of experience in quality, manufacturing, or engineering

Desired Characteristics & Experiences

- Excel proficiency
- Experience with First Article Inspection planning and execution
- Experience with drawing interpretation and blueprint review
- Experience performing dimensional inspection
- Experience working with turbine hardware
- Experience supporting manufacturing, quality, or engineering processes in an industrial environment
- Experience working across cross-functional teams to resolve technical and operational issues
- Familiarity with customer requirements and quality documentation processes
- Experience using ECAV or similar quality documentation systems
- Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn
- Transparent: shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively
- Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed
- Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative

Job Description

The First-Class CNC Machinist (CNC Lathes & Grinding) is responsible for advanced setup, operation, and troubleshooting of CNC turning and grinding processes to manufacture aerospace components to engineering drawings, specifications, and controlled process requirements. This role works with a high level of independence, maintains strict quality and traceability, and supports Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) through disciplined execution and continuous improvement.

At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. As a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft, we are at the forefront of advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Joining GE Aerospace means bringing your unique perspective, innovative spirit, drive, and curiosity to a collaborative and diverse team that values your ideas and listens to your voice. You will be part of our ongoing LEAN transformation, working smarter, not harder, and contributing to work that truly matters. Here, you will elevate your future, share in our pride and purpose, and make a real impact on the lives of millions around the globe. If you believe in the power of flight and want to be part of a spirited and collaborative team, come aboard and help us lead the way.

Individuals selected for this internship will have the responsibility and authority to carry out all assigned tasks.

Key Responsibilities

- Safety & compliance: Follow all EHS requirements, PPE, and safe machine operation practices; maintain an organized work area aligned to site standards.
- CNC lathe setup and operation: Perform complete independent setups on CNC turning centers (e.g., 2-axis and/or multi-axis with live tooling as applicable), including work holding/chucking, tooling setup, offsets, and first-piece validation.
- Grinding setup and operation: Set up and operate grinding equipment as applicable (e.g., OD/ID cylindrical grinding, surface grinding, centerless grinding); dress wheels, verify wheel selection/spec, and maintain process stability.
- Process execution and control: Run CNC programs and grinding cycles, make authorized offsets/adjustments, monitor tool/wheel wear and part growth, and maintain capable processes over production runs.
- Blueprint, GD&T interpretation, understanding of G code: Read and interpret routers, engineering drawings, GD&T, and inspection requirements to meet dimensional, concentricity/runout, and surface finish requirements, ability to make small changes in G Code.
- In-process inspection: Perform in-process and final inspection using precision measurement tools (e.g., micrometers, bore gages, indicators, height gages, profilometer/surface finish gage, thread gages as applicable). Document results per requirements.
- Troubleshooting and problem solving: Identify nonconformances (e.g., chatter, taper, lobing, burn, size drift, runout issues), stop work when required, escalate appropriately, and support containment and corrective actions.
- Documentation & traceability: Complete production and quality records accurately; maintain lot traceability, part identification, and required documentation/system transactions.
- Continuous improvement: Participate in kaizen/continuous improvement efforts to reduce scrap, rework, and cycle time; support standard work, 5S, and mistake-proofing (poka-yoke) initiatives.
- Equipment care (operator maintenance): Perform routine operator maintenance (cleaning, coolant concentration checks, basic TPM tasks) and promptly report abnormal machine conditions.

Required Qualifications

- Active Military personnel on their last 180 days of Military service
- High school diploma/GED/Vocational school certificate, with a minimum of 5 years machining experience in a manufacturing environment.
- Demonstrated ability to interpret engineering drawings and GD&T.
- Demonstrated CNC machining experience with the ability to perform independent setups on CNC lathes and/or grinding operations and/or multi-axis CNC turning and complex work holding, producing parts to tight tolerance.
- Strong understanding of turning and grinding fundamentals, tooling/wheel selection basics, fixturing/work holding, feeds/speeds, and process control.
- Inspection: Proficiency with precision measurement and recording results to requirements; ability to validate first-piece and monitor process capability.
- Experience collaborating with Manufacturing Engineering/Quality to support process improvements and corrective actions.
- Experience with FAI (e.g., AS9102)
- Ability to obtain and maintain a secret clearance
- This role may encounter high risk or hazardous operations and/or include working shifts beyond a standard workweek. As such, a requirement of the role is to be at least 18 years of age by the time of joining.

Desired Qualifications

- Aerospace manufacturing experience with controlled processes and strict documentation/traceability requirements
- Experience machining aerospace materials such as Ceramic Composites
- Experience in machining/precision components
- Experience with 3 and 5-axis vertical and horizonal machining center
