postings.description:
Job Description Summary
The AI Architect is the senior technical leader for the team building AI enabled engineering capabilities across the business organizations of an aero engine and propulsion OEM. The role sets the reference architecture, selects and sequences the use cases worth pursuing, validates feasibility through proof of concept builds, and leads and coaches the engineers who deliver them, ensuring everything the team ships is deliverable inside aerospace constraints on data, security, and export control. It pairs hands on technical ownership with the second line leadership, operating plan and budget ownership, and governance responsibilities of the Sr. Director, Architecture (SPB1) standard, with five AI Engineers, one aligned to each business, as direct reports (growing to include team leads), and the mandate to grow the function as the portfolio expands. Deep credibility in the physics and engineering of the product, turbomachinery, aerodynamics, combustion, heat transfer, structures, and materials, and a product mindset shaped by certified, safety critical hardware are core to the role; AI is applied to challenging propulsion and turbomachinery engineering problems across design, analysis, test, manufacturing, and sustainment, not treated as a specialty unto itself.

Job Description

In this role, you will:

- Lead and coordinate the technical and business discussions on future AI architectural direction across multiple teams and complex product lines, anchored to real propulsion and turbomachinery engineering problems.
- Analyze, design, and develop a roadmap and implementation plan for AI enabled engineering capabilities based on a current vs. future state, in a cohesive architecture viewpoint aligned to the digital thread.
- Review, analyze, and develop architecture at the domain level and across multiple teams, reference architectures for data pipelines, model and agent deployment, evaluation, and integration with PLM and existing simulation and analysis toolchains.
- Ground the reference architecture in the realities of aero engine, propulsion, and turbomachinery engineering, design, analysis (CFD, FEA, thermal and structural), test, manufacturing, and sustainment, defining how AI integrates with model based systems engineering, the digital thread, PLM, engine and rig test data, and the existing simulation toolchains.
- Participate in the enterprise architecture domain governance model, and define the AI governance, security, and export control posture (ITAR / export control, CMMC, RMF / ATO) so solutions are compliant by design across classified and unclassified environments.
- Contribute to the development of software, data, and technology platforms with reusable components across teams that can be orchestrated together, capturing reusable patterns, libraries, and reference implementations from each delivery.
- Lead the research and evaluation of emerging AI technology, industry, and market trends (LLM and retrieval augmented generation, vector databases, agentic orchestration) to inform development and operational support across multiple teams; run proof of concept builds to validate architectural and physical assumptions, including where physics informed or surrogate modeling of engine analysis (CFD/FEA/thermal) is appropriate versus where it is not, before committing the team.
- Set model and agent lifecycle practice: evaluation against engineering ground truth, versioning, monitoring, drift detection, retraining triggers, and rollback.
- Provide leadership, technology guidance, and mentorship throughout the domain; provide architecture direction to the embedded AI Engineers, review their designs, and remove technical blockers to keep delivery moving.
- Be a technical leader within the function and develop and coach the technical resources within it; serve as the single technical interface to enterprise platform, data, and security functions.
- Influence from a strategic and technical standpoint across the function and the business; present business and technical discipline solutions to senior leaders, communicate complex messages, and negotiate internally and with external partners, vendors, and customers to align on direction, tradeoffs, feasibility, and risk.
- Own and influence the budget and operating plan for the AI engineering function; provision and budget via capital and operating, and manage financials across programs and projects.
- Develop peer, cross functional, and cross business relationships to maximize best practice sharing and team effectiveness.
- Be responsible for management activities including recruiting, development, performance management, compensation, organization, and teaming.
- Lead the AI Engineering team, five AI Engineers, one aligned to each business, plus team leads as the function scales toward second line management, with the ability to attract, develop, and retain talent and to grow the team as the portfolio expands.
- Share technical, procedural, and business knowledge with others. Leverage your domain expertise to further the knowledge and improve the productivity of colleagues, creating learning content, giving presentations, and supporting a continuous learning culture.

Education Qualification

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a STEM major Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math)
- 10 years of experience, including production AI/ML systems, architecture at enterprise scale, and leadership of technical teams.
- This role requires the successful candidate to maintain a US Government Security Clearance; prerequisite for a security clearance is U.S Citizenship. Preference is given to candidates who currently hold a US Government Security Clearance.
- Legal authorization to use in the U.S is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening

Desired Characteristics

- Advanced Degree
- Technical Expertise
- Ability to consult with the business on the alignment of outcomes and desired AI technical solutions at an enterprise level.
- Ability to analyze, design, and develop an AI solution roadmap and implementation plan based on a current vs. future state of the business.
- Demonstrated architecture experience covering model training, deployment, and monitoring at enterprise scale, on a strong software engineering foundation: design patterns, APIs, integration approaches, cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP), and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).
- Hands on experience with LLM and retrieval augmented generation patterns, vector databases, and agentic orchestration frameworks.
- Working knowledge of configuration choices and related cost implications, compute, model hosting, and build vs. buy, and experience with complex solution configurations.
- Working knowledge of data engineering, data governance, and assessing data readiness for AI on messy, real engineering data.
- Experience sustaining operational stability through lifecycle phases (planning, implementation, steady state, decommissioning), including the model and agent (MLOps) lifecycle; ability to provision and budget via capital and operating.
- Experience delivering inside aerospace & defense or comparable regulated constraints: ITAR / export control, CMMC, RMF / ATO, and airgapped or impact level environments.
- Working fluency in the physics and engineering of aero engines and turbomachinery, aerodynamics, combustion, heat transfer, structures and rotordynamics, and materials, with the judgment to tell where a model is physically credible; familiarity with CFD, FEA, and thermal/structural simulation, engine and rig test data, surrogate and physics informed modeling, model based systems engineering, the digital thread, and PLM.
- Able to lead early stage interactions with domain engineering teams; guide them as they develop confidence and comfort with the approach and integrate it with their legacy tooling and investments.
- Leads others to find creative solutions within complex, interdependent engineering and production processes, drawing on multiple internal and external resources to evaluate conflicting information and arrive at decisions.

Business Acumen

- Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes, and services; stays informed of industry trends to inform decision making.
- Understands how the internal and external business model works, engine and propulsion programs, certification, and service / MRO, and facilitates active engagement.
- Able to articulate the value of what is most important to the business to achieve outcomes.
- Able to produce functional area information in sufficient detail for cross functional teams to use, applying presentation and storytelling concepts.
- A product mindset for safety critical, certified hardware: comfort with verification and validation, certification evidence, reliability, and the long product and service lifecycle of an engine program.
- Six Sigma Green Belt certification or equivalent quality certification.

Leadership

- Demonstrated working knowledge of the internal organization.
- Ability to foresee obstacles, identify workarounds, leverage resources, and rally teammates.
- Demonstrated ability to work with and/or lead blended teams, including third party partners and customer personnel.
- Demonstrated change management / acceleration capabilities.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including creativity and curiosity, with the ability to communicate and influence effectively across all organizational levels, and to lead without direct authority.
- Proven analytical and problem resolution skills.
- Ability to attract, hire, develop, and retain talent, including building and scaling a team of senior professionals and emerging team leads.
- Ability to influence and build consensus with other engineering, IT, and platform teams and leadership.

The base pay range for this position is $176,000-235,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. postings.location: Grand Rapids, Michigan, United States of America
postings.additional_locations: Clearwater, Florida, United States of America; Rockledge, Florida, United States of America
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
GE Aerospace is seeking an experienced Staff Engineer – FPGA Design/Verification to lead the development of custom logic for advanced avionics hardware. This role supports the full FPGA design lifecycle—from requirements and architecture through design, verification, documentation, and certification.

The successful candidate will bring strong FPGA design expertise, technical leadership, and the ability to manage multiple complex engineering efforts in a regulated aerospace environment. This individual will work across engineering teams to deliver reliable, certifiable custom-logic solutions for aviation applications.

Job Description

The Staff Engineer – FPGA Design/Verification will design, verify, and support FPGA, ASIC, and CPLD solutions used in avionics hardware. The role includes VHDL design and simulation, requirements development and traceability in DOORS, creation of DO-254 certification artifacts, and technical documentation throughout the product-development lifecycle.

This is a senior technical role requiring the ability to define complex architectures, develop project plans, manage schedule and cost objectives, support proposals, and lead work across multiple programs simultaneously. The engineer will use sound technical judgment to resolve challenging hardware and verification issues while mentoring less-experienced engineers and collaborating with cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities

- Perform engineering activities across the full FPGA design lifecycle, including requirements, architecture, design, simulation, verification, integration, and release.
- Design FPGA, ASIC, and CPLD solutions for aerospace and avionics hardware applications using Xilinx, Microsemi, Intel, Lattice, or comparable device families.
- Develop and maintain VHDL designs, simulation environments, and verification test benches.
- Develop, manage, and trace requirements in DOORS.
- Create and maintain technical data and certification artifacts in support of DO-254 and applicable civil or military aerospace requirements.
- Define FPGA/custom-logic architectures for complex product applications.
- Develop and execute custom-logic project plans, including technical scope, schedule, cost, risks, and resource requirements.
- Support bids, proposals, technical assessments, and product-development planning.
- Analyze technical data, conduct trade studies, and make design recommendations to support program decisions.
- Support hardware manufacturing, integration, troubleshooting, and technology-development activities as needed.
- Lead or support multiple projects and engineering teams in parallel.
- Provide technical guidance and mentorship to engineers with less experience.
- Communicate complex technical information clearly and build alignment across engineering, program, quality, and customer stakeholders.
- Ensure technical documentation is complete, accurate, and compliant with engineering policies and procedures.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline from an accredited university or college.
- Minimum of 8 years of professional design experience.
- Experience designing, developing, simulating, or verifying FPGA, ASIC, and/or CPLD hardware.
- Experience with VHDL-based FPGA design and simulation.
- Ability to develop technical plans, manage multiple priorities, and deliver work within program schedule and cost objectives.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Must be a U.S. citizen due to program and export-control requirements.

Desired Qualifications

- Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science Engineering, or a related discipline.
- At least 5 years of experience developing computing products containing complex System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures.
- Experience with Xilinx Zynq and/or Microchip PolarFire devices in System-on-Chip or System-on-Module applications.
- Knowledge of high-speed data interfaces and computing functions, including PCIe, AXI, SERDES, DMA, and related architectures.
- Experience with avionics interfaces and protocols, including MIL-STD-1553, ARINC 429, ARINC 664, and Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN).
- Experience with FPGA development environments such as Xilinx Vivado, Microchip Libero, Intel Quartus, and Lattice Diamond.
- Experience with VHDL and UVM test benches.
- Familiarity with Mentor Graphics tools, including Expedition Enterprise and HyperLynx PI/SI.
- Experience in military, aerospace, or avionics product development.
- Experience with DO-254 and civil FAA certification processes.
- Strong technical leadership, influence, facilitation, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
- Ability to break down complex technical problems, apply critical thinking, and drive practical solutions.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a senior FPGA engineer with deep experience designing and verifying complex custom logic for safety-critical or high-reliability hardware. They are confident working in VHDL, building verification environments, managing FPGA requirements and traceability in DOORS, and producing documentation needed for DO-254 certification.

They have practical experience with modern FPGA/SoC platforms and high-speed interfaces, ideally in an avionics, defense, or aerospace environment. Beyond technical depth, this person can lead work across several programs, define architecture and execution plans, guide junior engineers, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

This role requires access to U.S. export-controlled information. Therefore, employment will be contingent upon the ability to prove that you meet the status of a U.S. Person as one of the following: U.S. lawful permanent resident, U.S. Citizen, have been granted asylee or refugee status (i.e., a protected individual under the Immigration and Naturalization Act, 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)).

Job Description Summary
As Staff Engineer – Advanced Manufacturing, you will serve as a technical focal for rotating parts manufacturing and will support one of four core business areas: Small Turbine Disks; Medium Turbine Disks; Shafts and Spools; Seals. In this role, you will lead and develop advanced manufacturing solutions across both current-state production and future-state capability building, partnering closely with NC Programmers, CMM Programmers, and Methods Planners to drive CNC programming, inspection programming, process development, and project execution. You will help mature concurrent technologies, support NPI, new technology, and new equipment implementation, and lead larger-scale manufacturing projects that improve production readiness and performance. This role also offers the opportunity to influence the New Product Development Center by developing and proving out new processes with a dedicated team before transferring them into production cells.

Come and elevate your career in a facility that combines a rich tradition of aviation technology with a deep commitment to the future of flight. The GE Aerospace manufacturing site in Lynn designs, produces, assembles and tests military and commercial aircraft engines and components. With 1.6 million square feet of manufacturing space, we’re making a huge contribution to the future of flight. And, considering that the very first jet engines were born here in 1942, we clearly are the career home of people who are deeply knowledgeable about building quality engines. What’s more, GE Aerospace has invested more than $100 million in our facility in the last five years alone.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities

- Identify, develop, evaluate, and introduce advanced manufacturing solutions to meet current and future state production needs
- Lead and provide the key technical direction to large projects with critical business impact:
- Industrialize new rotating parts into the shop, including process routing definition, tooling and fixturing design, machining strategy, and inspection plans.
- Drive producibility reviews, DFM/DFA input, and process risk assessments.

- Lead the evaluation, selection, justification, and implementation of new machining, inspection, and automation equipment for rotating parts. Develop equipment specifications, support CapEx business cases, and lead runoffs, SAT/FAT, and production handoff.

- Develop, validate, and standardize robust machining processes for complex aerospace components. Optimize cycle time, tool life, and process capability while maintaining compliance with aerospace quality and regulatory standards.
- Provide technical consultation on product problems throughout the business
- Provide daily technical support to the shop for machining, set-up, and inspection issues. Lead root cause analysis and corrective action using structured problem-solving methods (8D, A3, fishbone, 5-Why).

- Provide technical guidance, direction and training to new and experienced materials engineers, specialists, technicians and co-ops

- Bachelor of Science in Engineering OR a HS Diploma/GED with 4 years of aerospace manufacturing and project management

- Experience balancing technical execution with project leadership, including equipment procurement, capital planning, and stakeholder communication
- Strong machining background in milling and turning of aerospace alloys such as nickel-based superalloys and titanium or other hard-to-machine aerospace alloys.
- Cylindrical grinding experience preferred
- Familiarity with inspection methods, standard gauging, and manufacturing quality requirements
- Experience with tooling, fixtures, NC programming, and process development
- Proficiency with Siemens NX (prior programming experience preferred) and Statistical Analysis in Minitab.
- Experience with Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or similar planning tools

- Ability to lead small teams and influence cross-functional partners without direct supervisory responsibility
- Strong communication, leadership, project management, and structured problem-solving skills
- Demonstrated ability to apply FLIGHT DECK principles to drive Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost in manufacturing environments
- Demonstrated alignment with GE Aerospace Behaviors: Respect for People, Continuous Improvement, and Customer-Driven Execution

À PROPOS DE GE AÉROSPATIAL :

Chez GE Aérospatial, nous faisons progresser les technologies aéronautiques d’aujourd’hui et de demain. Nous sommes l'un des principaux fournisseurs mondiaux de moteurs d'avion, de composantes et de systèmes intégrés pour les avions commerciaux et militaires. Spécifiquement, notre usine située à Bromont, se spécialise dans la fabrication des pièces des moteurs d’avion. Le site comporte un large volet manufacturier auquel s’annexent plusieurs axes de recherche et de développement. Depuis 2011, il comporte une équipe dédiée à l’intégraton et la fabrication des nouvelles composantes de compresseurs pour les moteurs du futur. Ce groupe effectue notamment la fabrication de pièces, la rétroaction manufacturière des plans et devis ainsi que la gestion de projets pour les futures générations de moteurs GE, ainsi que pour supporter l’amélioration de la flotte de moteurs actuellement en service.

CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS :

- Salaire concurrentiel et boni
- Horaire flexible
- Un service de cafétéria sur place
- Accès à des services de professionnels de la santé sur place: infirmière, médecin, kinésithérapeute et intervenante
- Possibilité de covoiturage

RÉSUMÉ DU RÔLE :

- Supporter les opérations de l’atelier
- Optimiser les systèmes de gestion des consommables
- Réviser les gammes d’usinage
- Effectuer le suivi des pièces et l’ordonnancement des opérations
- Créer et supporter les documents opérationnels
- La nature des mandats et des responsabilités sera appelée à varier selon l’expérience.

- Tu es une personne curieuse et motivée par le développement de nouveaux produits? Notre offre de stage est idéale pour toi. Nous fabriquons les composantes du futur via des procédés d’usinage 5 axes de haute précision dans un environnement dynamique et unique. Tu sera appelé(ée) à supporter notre atelier pour la planification des consommables, le suivi de nos produits et l’optimisation de nos processus de fabrication et de suivi des composantes.

QUALIFICATIFS REQUIS:

- Rapidité d’exécution et capacité d’apprentissage élevée.

postings.location: Saint-Eustache, Quebec, Canada
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Sous la supervision de l’équipe Qualité, le/la stagiaire Qualité assiste les techniciens qualité dans leurs activités quotidiennes afin de contribuer au contrôle de la qualité dans l’ensemble des opérations de production. Il/elle soutient notamment les activités d’inspection, de gestion des non-conformités, de calibration des équipements et de mise à jour de la documentation qualité, en respect des normes et procédures en vigueur.

Stage de 4 mois avec possibilité de 8 mois.

Job Description

Participer aux des projets d’amélioration continue et à l’amélioration du système de gestion de la qualité, en lien avec les activités ci-dessous

Support aux inspections et aux contrôles de la qualité

- Assister à l’inspection à la réception des matières premières, consommables et autres produits reçus au site selon le plan établi.
- Effectuer, sous supervision, des vérifications de produits afin de s’assurer de la conformité aux spécifications internes et clients.

Support à la gestion des non-conformités

- Aider à la saisie, au suivi et à la documentation des produits non conformes dans les systèmes appropriés.
- Contribuer à la préparation de rapports de non-conformité et au suivi des actions correctives et préventives, en collaboration avec l’équipe Qualité.

Support aux activités de calibration / métrologie

- Participer à la planification et au suivi des calibrations périodiques des instruments de mesure (mise à jour de registres, suivi des échéances).
- Supporter la calibration/vérification des équipements de production et de laboratoire selon le calendrier ou les demandes de production (ex. préparation des équipements, enregistrement des résultats).

Soutien au système de gestion de la qualité

- Contribuer à la mise à jour de la documentation qualité (procédures, formulaires, gabarits) sous la supervision de l’équipe.
- Participer, selon les besoins, à des projets d’amélioration continue et à l’amélioration du système de gestion de la qualité

Qualifications:

- Étudiant(e) au BACC (qualité, génie industriel, génie mécanique, métrologie ou domaine connexe)
- Aucune expérience obligatoire; un stage ou expérience en milieu manufacturier est un atout
- Compétences techniques
- Un atout : Connaissance de base en lecture de plans mécaniques
- Connaissance de base en utilisation d’instruments de mesure;
- Connaissances de base des principes qualité;
- Connaissance pratique de MS Office;
- Maîtrise du français (oral et écrit);

Job Description

GE Aérospatial est un acteur clé dans le secteur manufacturier, reconnu pour son engagement en matière d'innovation et d'amélioration continue des processus de production. Nous mettons un point d'honneur à développer nos collaborateurs et à investir dans des solutions optimisées pour notre environnement de travail.

Ici, vous aurez l’opportunité de travailler sur le futur de l'aviation avec les meilleurs dans le domaine. Un travail dont vous serez fier, et où les possibilités sont infinies. Chez GE Aérospatial, vous pouvez donner vie à vos idées dans un environnement collaboratif et innovant. Si vous avez la passion de transformer vos rêves en réalité, nous avons une

place pour vous!

- Travailler sur des CNC qui produisent des pièces d’une précision au millième;
- Développer la connaissance de différents procédés tel que, le traitement thermique et l’usinage chimique;
- D’assurer le bon fonctionnement des équipements de production en adoptant des mesures de prévention, de diagnostic des problèmes et de réparation;

Rémunération selon votre niveau de stage soit :

- T-1 : 21.42$/hr
- T-2 : 22.70$/hr
- T-3 : 24.09$/hr

Ce que nous offrons :

- Une certaine flexibilité d’horaire

- Vous faire connaitre dans une entreprise offrants d’excellentes conditions qui est en croissance et offrant des possibilités d’embauche après vos études

• … fabricant de plus de 3 millions d’aubes annuellement;

• … une usine avec plus de 250 robots et plus de 200 machines de mesure tridimensionnelle (MMT).

• … l’hôte du Centre d’excellence mondial en robotisation et automatisation;

• … reconnus pour notre efficacité, notre ingéniosité et notre capacité technique.

• … situés dans un environnement enchanteur, à Bromont (1h de Montréal).

Job Description Summary
Avio Aero, część GE Aerospace, to firma działająca w branży lotniczej, specjalizująca się w projektowaniu, produkcji i obsłudze komponentów oraz systemów do silników lotniczych. Do naszego zespołu finansów w zakładzie w Bielsku-Białej szukamy osoby, która chce zdobyć praktyczne doświadczenie w księgowości w międzynarodowym środowisku i poznać, jak funkcjonuje obszar księgi głównej w dużej organizacji.

Job Description

Na czym będzie polegać staż?

- Księgowaniu dokumentów w obszarze księgi głównej.
- Dokonywaniu uzgodnień kont i sald księgi głównej.
- Udziale w procesach związanych z wystawianiem faktur sprzedaży.
- Przygotowywaniu i uzgadnianiu dokumentów związanych ze zwrotami do dostawców.
- Wsparciu zespołu w przygotowywaniu danych do deklaracji VAT.
- Pomocy w przygotowywaniu raportów i deklaracji do GUS oraz NBP.

Będziesz pracować z doświadczonym zespołem, który pokaże Ci praktyczną stronę rachunkowości, zamknięcia miesiąca, uzgodnień kont oraz współpracy finansów z innymi działami firmy.

Kogo szukamy?

- Studentki/studenta lub absolwentki/absolwenta kierunku finanse i rachunkowość, ekonomia lub pokrewnego.
- Osoby komunikującej się w języku angielskim w stopniu pozwalającym na codzienną współpracę i pracę z dokumentami. Bardzo dobra znajomość języka polskiego w mowie i piśmie jest warunkiem koniecznym.
- Osoby dobrze znającej pakiet Microsoft Office, w szczególności Excel.
- Osoby dokładnej, zaangażowanej, dobrze zorganizowanej i chętnej do nauki.
- Osoby, która będzie dyspozycyjna w pełnym wymiarze czasu (5 dni w tygodniu, przeciętnie 8 h dziennie).

- Podstawowa znajomość zasad rachunkowości i podatku VAT.

postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Le ou la Superviseur(e) de maintenance est responsable de planifier, coordonner et superviser les activités de maintenance des équipements, des systèmes utilitaires et des bâtiments de l’usine. La personne titulaire du poste veille au bon fonctionnement des équipements critiques, notamment les tours d’eau et les systèmes de refroidissement, et contribue à la fiabilité des installations, à l’optimisation de la maintenance préventive ainsi qu’à la maîtrise des coûts d’entretien.

Job Description

Responsabilités principales

- Planifier, coordonner et superviser les travaux de maintenance corrective et préventive.
- Prioriser les interventions selon leur impact sur la production, la santé-sécurité et la qualité.
- Assurer le bon fonctionnement des équipements critiques, incluant les tours d’eau, systèmes de refroidissement et autres services utilitaires.
- Développer, mettre à jour et optimiser les programmes de maintenance préventive.
- Analyser les pannes, participer aux analyses de causes racines et mettre en place les actions correctives requises.
- Superviser l’entretien général des bâtiments et des systèmes connexes, tels que l’éclairage, le HVAC, la plomberie et les compresseurs d’air.
- Élaborer et suivre le budget de maintenance, tout en contribuant à l’optimisation des coûts.
- Encadrer, mobiliser et développer l’équipe de maintenance.
- Assurer le respect des normes, procédures et pratiques en matière de santé, sécurité, environnement et conformité réglementaire.
- Maintenir à jour la documentation technique, les historiques d’entretien et les données liées aux interventions.
- Participer aux initiatives d’amélioration continue visant la fiabilité, la disponibilité des équipements et la performance globale des opérations.

Profil recherché

- Leadership mobilisateur et capacité à encadrer une équipe.
- Bon sens de l’organisation et capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités.
- Solides aptitudes en analyse, résolution de problèmes et prise de décision.
- Forte orientation santé-sécurité.
- Capacité à collaborer efficacement avec plusieurs départements.

Exigences

- Diplôme technique en maintenance industrielle, électromécanique, génie mécanique ou dans une discipline connexe
- De 5 à 10 ans d’expérience en gestion de la maintenance dans un environnement manufacturier.
- De 3 à 5 ans d’expérience en supervision ou coordination d’équipe.
- Bonne connaissance des systèmes de refroidissement industriels, tours d’eau et équipements utilitaires.
- Capacité à lire et interpréter des plans, schémas et diagrammes techniques.
- Connaissance d’une GMAO, un atout.
- Maîtrise du français, à l’oral et à l’écrit.
- Vu les interactions courantes nécessitant la lecture de documents techniques ainsi que des communications simples à l’extérieur du Canada, une connaissance de niveau fonctionnel à intermédiaire, à l’oral et à l’écrit, est requise;

Conditions particulières

- Disponibilité pour répondre à des urgences opérationnelles, au besoin.
- Présence requise en usine selon les besoins des opérations.

Job Description Summary
The Systems Engineer – Product Integration is responsible for driving cross-functional systems engineering activities across the product lifecycle, from concept and design through production and operation. This role ensures business and technical requirements are translated into integrated system solutions that meet customer needs, performance expectations, and quality standards. The position supports product and component integration, requirements management, interface definition, validation and verification planning, risk management, and configuration control. This role impacts departmental execution and requires strong technical judgment, collaboration, and disciplined execution within established engineering practices.

The location for this position is Grand Rapids, MI on at least a hybrid basis (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday in office) : An extensive corporate relocation package is also available for eligible candidates.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Lead and support system integration activities across components, modules, and products to ensure maximum system performance, operability, and compliance.
- Manage system and product requirements, including development, flow down, traceability, and alignment across component owners, suppliers, subcontractors, and partner teams.
- Drive validation and verification activities for the overall product or system, including system-level test planning, execution support, and closure of verification evidence.
- Define and communicate product requirements for modules, components, subcontractors, and external partners.
- Manage interfaces between components, teams, and execution organizations to ensure integrated product development and successful program execution.
- Drive CTQ and risk trades with design teams to balance technical performance, quality, cost, and schedule.
- Maintain oversight of the overall product configuration, including support for configuration management and configuration control processes.
- Apply technical knowledge and prior experience to execute engineering work in alignment with established policies, strategies, and business objectives.
- Work across teams and functions to support planning, execution, issue resolution, and on-time delivery of engineering commitments.
- Use sound judgment and analytical thinking to evaluate options, solve technical problems, and escalate issues as needed.
- Provide informal guidance and technical support to less experienced team members and contribute to a collaborative team environment.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college in Engineering or a related technical discipline; or a high school diploma / GED with at least 6 years of experience in a relevant engineering or technical function.
- Experience in systems engineering, product integration, requirements management, validation and verification, or related technical disciplines.
- Demonstrated ability to work across functions and coordinate technical activities involving multiple teams and stakeholders.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- This position requires U.S. citizenship status.

Desired Characteristics

- Strong oral and written communication skills.
- Demonstrated ability to analyze issues, develop solutions, and drive closure.
- Ability to document plans, coordinate activities, and execute programs with discipline.
- Experience with requirements management, interface management, system integration, and configuration control.
- Established project management or program coordination skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional, team-based engineering environment.
- Demonstrated technical curiosity and willingness to build depth in a specific engineering discipline.

postings.title: T700/CT7 Depot Subject Matter Expert – Quality / Repair Engineering (w/m/x)
postings.location: Warsaw, Masovian, Poland
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Depot Subject Matter Expert provides depot-level technical expertise for T700/CT7 engine maintenance, repair, inspection, assembly/disassembly, troubleshooting, and test activities. This role supports both hands-on shop execution and quality/engineering-focused evaluation of maintenance activities, ensuring work is performed in accordance with technical directives, approved procedures, and operational requirements. This role also helps develop workforce capability by coaching and training customer personnel on quality systems, supporting documentation, workstation development, heavy machine operation, and technical discipline.

GE Aerospace is seeking a T700/CT7 (Turboshaft) Depot Subject Matter Expert - Quality / Repair Engineering to provide technical leadership across depot maintenance activity for T700/CT7 engines and modules. In this role, you will help interpret maintenance directives, evaluate maintenance activity for compliance and completeness, support troubleshooting and repair decisions, and strengthen documentation, training, and process discipline. This is a hands-on technical role for a professional who can connect quality expectations with practical depot execution. This role is full time, on-site at customer facility located in Deblin, Poland.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

- Interpret and apply technical directives, manuals, drawings, wiring diagrams, schematic diagrams, and maintenance publications relevant to T700/CT7 depot operations.
- Review maintenance activity to verify procedural compliance, technical accuracy, inspection completeness, and alignment to approved instructions.
- Assist with troubleshooting engine and module conditions by studying technical data, maintenance findings, and engine operating characteristics.
- Support determination of work scope and repair procedures for T700-GE-701C/D, CT7-2E1, and CT7-8E engines, modules, and components based on technical requirements and condition assessment.
- Partner with GE internal and customer operations, quality, and engineering teams to resolve technical questions and reinforce standardized maintenance execution.
- Help ensure maintenance records, findings, inspections, and related documentation are complete, accurate, compliant, and usable.
- Provide technical support across inspection, repair, modification, assembly, disassembly, and test-related activities as needed.
- Deliver on-the-job training and practical guidance to customer personnel to build technical capability and reinforce process compliance.
- Identify quality risks, recurring issues, or process gaps and support corrective action and continuous improvement efforts.
- Support proper use of tooling, support equipment, preservation requirements, and handling practices where quality oversight is needed.

Basic Qualifications

- Demonstrated experience in T700/CT7 engine maintenance, depot operations, or closely related turboshaft engine maintenance support.
- Ability to interpret technical manuals, drawings, wiring diagrams, schematic diagrams, and maintenance instructions.
- Strong troubleshooting capability and experience supporting technical evaluation of defects, maintenance findings, and repair decisions.
- Experience with engine or module inspection, assembly, disassembly, repair, and test activity as relevant to depot operations.
- Working knowledge of maintenance documentation, procedural compliance, and quality-focused execution in a controlled environment.
- Experience using applicable tools, special tools, and test equipment associated with turboshaft engine maintenance activity.
- Ability to provide effective on-the-job training, technical coaching, and clear written or verbal guidance.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with quality systems, maintenance process compliance, engineering support, or technical publication implementation.
- Background in work instruction validation, maintenance evaluation, audit support, or inspection documentation review.
- Experience supporting military, depot, or sustainment programs with disciplined configuration and procedural control.
- Demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement utilizing FLIGHT DECK or similar lean operating system, corrective action follow-through, and practical process standardization.
- Ability to work effectively across quality, engineering, operations, and customer-facing teams to solve technical issues.
- Experience coaching teams on documentation quality, process discipline, and repeatable execution.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means helping the depot team produce technically sound, procedurally compliant, and well-documented maintenance outcomes. You will bring structure to complex technical work, support confident repair decisions, build capability through training, and help ensure quality expectations are consistently translated into daily execution. Customer will take away a continuous improvement mindset, with the ability to properly utilize and implement FLIGHT DECK tools in response to shop identified concerns.

RÉSUMÉ DU RÔLE :

À PROPOS DE GE AÉROSPATIAL :

Chez GE Aérospatial, nous faisons progresser les technologies aéronautiques d’aujourd’hui et de demain. Nous sommes l'un des principaux fournisseurs mondiaux de moteurs d'avion, de composantes et de systèmes intégrés pour les avions commerciaux et militaires. Spécifiquement, notre usine située à Bromont, se spécialise dans la fabrication des pièces des moteurs d’avion. Le site offre un environnement de travail dynamique alliant l’automatisation et la robotisation et une culture de gestion participative.

CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS :

· Salaire concurrentiel et boni annuel

· Minimum de 3 semaines de vacances dès l’embauche en plus de 7 jours payés durant le temps des fêtes

· Régime d’assurance collective incluant des services de télémédecine et programmes de santé et mieux-être dont un remboursement aux frais de conditionnement physique

· Régime de retraite à cotisations déterminées

· Un service de cafétéria sur place

· Accès à des services de professionnels de la santé sur place: infirmière, médecin, kinésithérapeute et intervenante

· Rabais pour le magasin des employés sur les électroménagers GE.

RÉSUMÉ DU RÔLE :

Nous recherchons idéalement un.e candidat.e possédant une solide expérience en programmation CMM. Cela dit, nous sommes également ouvert à considérer des candidat.es ayant moins d’expérience et démontrant un fort potentiel, qui pourront être accompagnés et formés au sein de l’équipe.

À titre de membre de l’équipe du service de métrologie, vous fournirez l’expertise technique et le soutien nécessaires à l’atteinte des objectifs opérationnels des équipes de production et d’outillage. Dans une approche client-fournisseur, vous aurez notamment les responsabilités suivantes :

- Développer et mettre en place des routines d’inspection sur différents instruments de mesure, principalement des CMM.
- Offrir un soutien technique lors de mises en course complexes ou dans le cadre du développement de nouvelles technologies.
- Optimiser les routines d’inspection existantes ainsi que les procédés de programmation associés.
- Améliorer la rapidité et l’efficacité des méthodes de travail et de programmation grâce à une approche de standardisation.
- Contribuer au développement et à la mise en application d’une vision stratégique et technique en matière de métrologie.
- Participer au travail d’équipe en offrant du coaching et de la formation sur différents outils, selon le niveau d’expérience à l’entrée en poste.
- Proposer des solutions d’amélioration pour les inspections et la mise en œuvre des procédés de fabrication.
- Déboguer des programmes ou intervenir sur des équipements en cours de production.

PROFIL IDÉAL :

Nous recherchons idéalement une personne possédant une expérience significative en programmation CMM dans un environnement industriel de précision, mais nous invitons également les candidatures de personnes moins expérimentées ayant une bonne base technique, une forte capacitée d’apprentissage et l’intérêt de se développer dans ce domaine.

QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES

- Détenir une formation professionelle ou collégiale dans un domaine pertinent, ou posséder une expérience en programmation CMM dans un milieu industriel de précision.

- Pour les profils expérimentés : être en mesure de développer de façon autonome des programmes d’inspection et de programmer la vérification de pièces complexes.
- Pour les profils en développement : démontrer une bonne base technique et le potentiel nécessaire pour évoluer vers l’autonomie avec accompagnement et formation.
- Maîtriser, ou avoir la capacité de développer rapidement, les compétences liées au tolérancement géométrique, à la lecture de plans, ainsi qu’à la conception de jauges, gabarits et montages.
- Avoir de bonnes aptitudes en résolution de problèmes et un esprit d’analyse développé.
- Être à l’aise avec les notions de paramétrisation de programmes, les concepts de vecteurs et les fonctions trigonométriques.
- Posséder de bonnes connaissances d’un logiciel de CAO.
- Avoir une compréhension générale des systèmes qualité en aéronautique.

Souhaitées :

- Vu les interactions occasionnelles avec l'équipe globale située à l’extérieur du Canada, la compréhension de base de l’anglais – oral et écrit – est souhaitée

Que nous fabriquions des composantes pour nos moteurs ou que nous innovions en matière de carburant et de réduction de bruit, nos équipes de GE Aérospatial sont dévouées et ont un impact mondial. Rejoignez-nous, voyez vos idées prendre leur envol et aidez à faire progresser l’industrie aérospatiale.

postings.title: Test Systems Technical Lead
postings.location: Cheltenham, Gloucestershire, United Kingdom
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
As a Test Systems Technical Lead, you will be responsible for the technical direction, definition, and delivery of test system solutions across Power Distribution and Controls programs. You will own the technical solution for your product/project area, ensuring that test systems meet Safety, Quality, customer, regulatory, and business requirements while supporting program Delivery and Cost objectives.

Working as part of an Integrated Product Development Team (IPDT), you will lead the full test systems lifecycle from initial requirements capture through design, implementation, verification, release, and in-service support. You will demonstrate strong technical leadership, collaborate closely with Program and Engineering Project Managers, and provide guidance, coaching, and mentoring to engineers in the test systems team.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

1. Test Systems Lifecycle Ownership

Own the technical solution for test systems in your product/project area, ensuring alignment to customer, regulatory, and internal requirements. Lead the full Test Systems life cycle from concept and requirements definition through design, implementation, verification, formal release, and in-service support. Execute requirements, design, implementation, and verification using sound engineering principles, adhering to business standards, procedures, and program requirements. Ensure test equipment solutions are suitable for qualification, EMC, system verification, and production support, in line with DO-160, MIL-STD-461 and similar standards.

2. Technical Leadership

Own the technical direction and accountability for test systems within your project to meet customer and derived requirements. Monitor and steer the technical solution, ensuring rigor in design and technical reviews for your test solution. Collaborate with the Designated Technical Authority (DTA) to ensure test system architectures and strategies are aligned to the overall product architecture. Engage SMEs and Chief Engineer’s Office as needed to resolve complex technical issues, de-risk solutions, and ensure compliance with internal design guidelines. Ensure adherence to project plans, company and industry standards, and appropriate application of DTC (Design to Cost) and DFM (Design for Manufacture) / DFT (Design for Test) principles for test solutions.

3. Budget / Schedule / Scope Support

Support the Control Account Manager (CAM) and EPM in delivering the technical solution to the agreed scope, schedule, and budget for your project. Protect against internal and external scope creep for the test system, identifying potential changes early and supporting mitigation. Clearly communicate technical expectations to the engineering team, including definition of done, entry/exit criteria, and required deliverables. Support work package planning (e.g., rolling wave planning, milestones, and estimates) and provide input to technical metrics to monitor progress and health of test activities. Provide timely technical inputs to program reviews, Toll Gates, forecast updates, and risk & opportunity reviews as requested by EPM/PM.

4. Cross-functional Collaboration and Customer Interface

Act as the engineering interface to Program Management on test systems topics, clearly articulating technical direction, risks, and decisions. Liaise and interface with Systems, Hardware, Software, Manufacturing, Sustaining, Quality, Supply Chain, and Lab Operations to ensure integrated and robust test solutions. Support Program Manager and EPM in customer and certification discussions related to test system capability, coverage, readiness, and evidence. Ensure alignment and coordination with Manufacturing Program Manager (Launch Leader) and production test stakeholders regarding test strategy, manufacturability, and transition to production test environments.

5. Governance, Documentation, and Compliance

Assure proper documentation of technical data generated for test systems in line with engineering policies, configuration control, and quality requirements. Ensure test system requirements, design artefacts, verification evidence, and configuration baselines are defined, maintained, and traceable. Participate as presenter or reviewer in technical, design, and program reviews (including CEO/DTA reviews where applicable), ensuring issues, risks, and lessons learned are captured and addressed. Support change management activities for test systems, providing technical impact assessments for scope/schedule changes and feeding into program BCRs as required.

6. People Leadership, Coaching and Behaviours

Provide technical guidance and leadership to engineers and technicians working on test systems, ensuring clarity of priorities, deliverables, and standards. Coach, mentor, and train less experienced engineers, actively building technical capability and succession in the test systems community. Model and reinforce GE Leadership Behaviours – Act with Humility, Lead with Transparency, Deliver with Focus – and the supporting core values of Leading, Influencing, and Collaborating. Demonstrate and promote key team behaviours, including risk identification and mitigation, proactive information sharing, collaborative decision making, constructive feedback, problem solving, and driving Lean and cost out. Provide timely communications on significant technical issues or developments and use the defined escalation paths (Tech Lead/CAM → EPM → Subsection Manager/PMO → PM → senior leadership) where resolution is blocked or risks escalate.

Required Qualifications

Degree in Electrical, Electronic, or Software Engineering, or equivalent knowledge and experience. Significant experience in test system design, development, and integration, including hardware/software integration for complex systems, ideally in aviation or other high integrity/safety-critical environments. Demonstrated experience in qualification and EMC test equipment design, with working knowledge/awareness of DO-160, MIL-STD-461 or equivalent environmental and EMC standards.

Proven technical leadership experience delivering solutions to agreed scope, schedule, cost, and quality, preferably as a Technical Lead, CAM, or equivalent within a project environment. Strong problem-solving and solution-building skills, with the ability to break down complex problems, identify options, and drive to resolution.

Excellent communication skills, able to clearly convey complex technical topics to engineering teams, program management, customers, and leadership. Evidence of independent and sound technical judgement, including identifying when to escalate and when to seek DTA/CEO guidance.

Desired Characteristics

Demonstrable success in achieving and exceeding customer and program milestones for test system or product deliveries. Proven ability to deliver solutions on time, within budget, and to the required quality, operating effectively across TG3–TG9 project phases. Positive attitude, initiative, and proactiveness, with enthusiasm for continuous improvement, Lean thinking, and cost-out in test solutions. Experience mentoring and developing engineers, including delegating technical work, providing feedback, and supporting career development. Experience with aircraft power distribution systems verification laboratories or similar system integration/verification environments. Ability to gather support from multiple stakeholders and influence cross-functional teams, leveraging strong product and architecture understanding. Demonstrated collaboration across global, multi-function teams, creating environments where customer-centric creativity and outside-in thinking are encouraged.

Leadership Behaviours & Expectations

The Test Systems Technical Lead is expected to:

- Lead complex, cross-functional technical workstreams within programs, often spanning multiple products or platforms.
- Serve as the primary technical escalation point for test systems in their area, while using defined escalation paths for unresolved issues.
- Set high standards for safety, quality, and compliance, and actively drive continuous improvement in test strategies, methods, and tools.
- Act with humility, lead with transparency, and deliver with focus, always with unyielding integrity.

Flexible Working

GE Aerospace supports and encourages flexible working arrangements, where possible, and recognises the benefits to employees of having a positive work-life balance.

Total Reward

At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.

As a new joiner to GE Aerospace we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs;

- Non-contributory Pension

- Life Assurance

- Group income protection

- Private medical cover

- Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible option to buy or sell

Security Clearance

Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS

Right to Work

Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

postings.title: Testing Specialist
postings.location: Dayton, Ohio, United States of America
postings.description:
Job Description Summary
GE Aerospace is seeking a hands-on Testing Specialist to support the validation of advanced aerospace electrical-power generation and conversion products. Based at the EPISCenter in Dayton, Ohio—the headquarters for Aerospace Power Engineering—this role supports development activities for technologies such as hybrid-electric aircraft, military platforms, and silicon-carbide (SiC) power systems.

The EPISCenter includes a 155,000-square-foot laboratory with seven high-power test cells totaling 15 MW, an EMI chamber, electronics and rapid-prototype labs, and real-time simulation capabilities. This is an opportunity for a technically capable test professional to work directly with advanced electrical and mechanical systems in a large-scale engineering test environment.

Job Description

The Testing Specialist performs laboratory and field validation testing, inspections, and data acquisition in support of aerospace electrical-power products and services. This role is responsible for setting up and operating test equipment, building test rigs and instrumentation systems, executing approved test procedures, collecting high-quality test data, and supporting troubleshooting activities.

Working with engineering, EHS, quality, planning, and materials teams, the Testing Specialist helps ensure tests are executed safely, accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with applicable procedures and technical documentation. The successful candidate brings strong electrical and mechanical aptitude, practical troubleshooting ability, and a commitment to safe, disciplined lab operations.

Key Responsibilities

- Execute laboratory and field validation tests, inspections, and data-acquisition activities supporting aerospace electrical-power generation and conversion products.
- Set up, operate, monitor, and maintain test equipment, test cells, instrumentation, and data-acquisition systems.
- Support the design and construction of test facilities, test rigs, instrumentation systems, and test software.
- Read, understand, and strictly follow test plans, test procedures, equipment operating procedures, quality-control documents, maintenance manuals, and shop manuals.
- Partner with engineering teams on test setup, test execution, troubleshooting, and documentation of test results.
- Use sound electrical and mechanical judgment to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve issues within established procedures.
- Collaborate with EHS, quality, planning, materials, and engineering teams to meet site safety, quality, operational, and continuous-improvement objectives.
- Collect, organize, inspect, and communicate accurate test data and observations to support product design and validation decisions.
- Support safe and efficient operation of high-power laboratory equipment and test environments.
- Work independently within established guidance and escalate complex issues to senior team members as appropriate.
- Be available to support testing outside regular first-shift hours, including occasional evenings and weekends, as program needs require.

Basic Qualifications

- High school diploma or GED.
- Minimum of 7 years of relevant technical experience in a testing, laboratory, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, maintenance, aerospace, automotive, military, or similar environment.
- Hands-on experience operating, setting up, maintaining, or troubleshooting electrical and/or mechanical equipment.
- Ability to read and follow detailed technical procedures, operating instructions, maintenance manuals, and safety requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to work safely and make sound technical decisions in a fast-paced hands-on environment.
- Ability to support testing outside standard first-shift hours and on weekends when needed.

Desired Qualifications

- Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Automation, or a related field, with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
- Familiarity with electrical-power systems used in commercial or military aircraft.
- Experience with high-power electrical equipment, power conversion, generators, motors, inverters, or power-distribution systems.
- Experience with data-acquisition systems, sensors, instrumentation, test automation, or test-software development.
- Experience designing, building, or modifying test rigs, test fixtures, instrumentation systems, or lab test setups.
- Strong electrical and mechanical aptitude, with a demonstrated interest in continued technical learning.
- Ability to interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and technical manuals.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document test work clearly and accurately.
- Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and ability to work independently or as part of a cross-functional team.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a hands-on test professional who enjoys working around complex electrical and mechanical equipment and wants to support the development of next-generation aerospace power technologies. They are comfortable setting up tests, connecting instrumentation, operating equipment, capturing data, following detailed procedures, and troubleshooting issues as they arise.

They bring a safety-first mindset, strong electrical and mechanical fundamentals, and practical experience in a laboratory, test-cell, manufacturing, maintenance, field-service, or military environment. They collaborate well with engineers but can independently execute assigned work, recognize when an issue needs escalation, and maintain precise documentation throughout the test process.

This role requires access to U.S. export-controlled information. Therefore, employment will be contingent upon the ability to prove that you meet the status of a U.S. Person as one of the following: U.S. lawful permanent resident, U.S. Citizen, have been granted asylee or refugee status (i.e., a protected individual under the Immigration and Naturalization Act, 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)).

Job Description Summary
Our Lynn, MA team is looking to hire a Tig Welder to perform layout, set-up and welding on a variety of aircraft engine component parts and assemblies. In this role you can expand your career welding various exotic materials into critical parts for commercial and/or military aircraft. You will receive training to achieve necessary certifications on required processes to set you up for success and ensure that you are working at required quality and efficiency levels.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace

If you want to do work that really matters among a team of spirited and collaborative individuals, you need to know more about GE Aerospace. We’ve become a world leader in the design, development and manufacture of advanced aviation technologies including jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We’re a people-first organization that will bring out your best ideas and performance as part of our on-going LEAN transformation. We believe that the world works better when it flies. Do you? If so, come aboard.

Working at our Lynn Facility

Come and elevate your career in a facility that combines a rich tradition of aviation technology with a deep commitment to the future of flight. The GE Aerospace manufacturing site in Lynn designs, produces, assembles, and tests military and commercial aircraft engines and components. With more 2,500 employees and 1.6 million sqft of manufacturing space, we’re making a huge contribution to the future of flight. And, considering that very first jet engines were born here in 1942, we clearly are the career home of people who are deeply knowledgeable about building quality engines. What’s more, GE Aerospace has invested more than $100 million in our facility in the last five years alone.

By engaging with highly collaborative teams, we’re reaching for new Sustainable Aviation Fuel milestones every year. And by encouraging our teams to join us in extensive community service and volunteerism, we’re making a difference in all the ways that matter.

Here are just a few of the best reasons you will want to consider us:

- Do work with a real purpose helping to solve the global challenge of how the world flies more sustainably.
- Be a part of a global workforce of diverse backgrounds, perspectives, ideas, and experiences where everyone feels supported and respected.
- Earn merit-based rewards and incentives.
- Free Onsite Parking.
- Set work schedule with no mandatory overtime.
- Work in a climate-controlled building out of the elements.
- Have opportunities for continuous learning and development.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- High School Diploma/GED
- 1 year of TIG welding experience in a manufacturing environment or have successfully completed a welding co-op or course with a certified agent
- Must be able to pass initial welding skills demonstration
- Able to work from planning and verbal instructions, prints or sketches require the ability to read, write, and speak English.
- Distance Vision 20/30 (US) using corrected or uncorrected vision in either eye
- Near Vision corrected or uncorrected in either eye, shall be the ability to read Jaeger No. 2 type at 16 inches (40.64 cm)
- Ability to lift, move and manipulate fixtures and component hardware up to 25 lbs. with or without reasonable accommodations
- $1000 Dollar sign on bonus for qualified candidates!

This role may encounter high risk or hazardous operations, working with chemicals, and/or include working shifts beyond a standard workweek. As such, a requirement of the role is to be at least 18 years of age by the time of joining.

Desired Characteristics:

- Previous welding and fabrication experience on aerospace hardware
- Previous held weld certification(s) in: corrosive resistant and heat resistant ferrous alloys, nickel base alloys, cobalt-base alloys, aluminum alloys, and titanium alloys

Aviation is a world-leading provider of jet and turboprop engines, as well as integrated systems for commercial, military, business and general aviation aircraft. Also, partnering with NASA and other leaders, GE Aviation is working to accelerate the introduction of hybrid electric flight technologies for commercial aviation. For more than 100 years, GE Aviation has worked to invent the future of flight and that work continues today.

The Production Supervisor is responsible for overseeing manufacturing processes, ensuring that production schedules are met, and maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). This role requires a deep understanding of manufacturing operations, strong leadership abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement. In this role, you will contribute to the production of advanced electrical components, modules and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft and vehicles as well as other mission systems. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and our unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Our facility in Pompano Beach, FL specializes in producing high-quality electrical power systems, and other aerospace technologies that support both commercial and military aircraft, ground vehicles and other military and electrical power systems. The site contributes to GE Aerospace's mission of delivering innovative solutions that prioritize safety, quality, and reliability in all we do.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Ensure compliance with all safety regulations and promote a culture of safety within the team.
- Accountable for the safety of your direct employees, and responsible for ensuring the environment is safe and all safe practices are followed.

- Demonstrated knowledge of new production introduction and low-rate production launch
- Ability to read and translate Engineering drawings to assist assemblers during first time builds of products
- Experience in the aerospace and/or automotive industry

- Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes and best practices
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills

postings.description:
Job Description Summary
Senior production quality leader over the manufacturing process for the Vandalia GE Aerospace site. Drives the quality function’s positive impact on Safety, Quality, Delivery and Cost in that order and timeliness of objectives. The role is subject to the standard operating procedures and policies of the Company , to include high standards for integrity and compliance. There is moderate autonomy within the role. High levels of operational judgment and strong business acumen are required to achieve quality objectives and adequately support business outcomes.

Job Description

About GE Aerospace:

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Working at our Vandalia Facilities:

Our Vandalia facility is located 50 minutes north of the GE Aerospace headquarters and sits just north of the city of Dayton—known widely as the birthplace of aviation—where the Wright Brothers built the world’s first aircraft in their bicycle shop in the heart of downtown Dayton. This business boasts a rich history, in operation for over 100 years. At over 140,000 square feet, the Vandalia facility rests on 27 acres right off Interstate 75.

At GE Aerospace in Vandalia, we specialize in manufacturing and servicing world-class power generation and electrical control and distribution equipment for a variety of military and commercial customers. Vandalia is also home to a product development lab where operators and engineers work together to invent the future of flight.

Role Overview

Senior production quality leader over the manufacturing process for the Vandalia GE Aerospace site. Drives the quality function’s positive impact on Safety, Quality, Delivery and Cost in that order and timeliness of objectives. The role is subject to the standard operating procedures and policies of the Company , to include high standards for integrity and compliance. There is moderate autonomy within the role. High levels of operational judgment and strong business acumen are required to achieve quality objectives and adequately support business outcomes.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Owns quality assurance and quality control, with a vision to creating a zero-defect culture. Includes quality assurance of products, services, manufacturing processes. Includes conformance in manufacturing, incoming goods control, product inspection, witness points, cost of poor quality, defects, etc.
- Manages a large team of quality professionals. Requires specialized knowledge of safety and quality within the function. Influence the development of strategy for the areas of responsibility, including control of resources and influencing policy formulation.
- Interprets simple internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes and services. Stays informed of industry trends that may inform their work and that of the greater quality function.
- Use high level of judgment to make decisions and handle complex tasks or problems in areas of operation, product management, manufacturing, technology or engineering. Has ability to assess quality of information given and ask pertinent questions to stakeholders. Able to offer new solutions to problems outside of set parameters and can construct and provide recommendations. Uses multiple internal and some external sources outside of own function to help arrive at a decision.
- Leads cross-functional teams and projects with minimal resource requirements, risk, and/or complexity. Communicates difficult concepts and may influence others on specific topics. Guides others to consider a different point of view.
- Drives cross-functional collaboration across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and the customer-facing Programs team to proactively address quality risks, accelerate problem resolution, and enable successful site and program performance.

Required Qualifications

- Master's degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma / GED with at least 6 years of experience in Manufacturing Operations, and/or Production Quality.)

Desired Characteristics

- Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems. Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects. Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs. Established project management skills.
- Engineering background and knowledge in quality audits, preferably aerospace.
- Proven track-record of doing the right thing under pressure.
- Past success with influence others through clear communication, use of data and reporting, and project/change management best practices.
- Attention to detail, with a continuous improvement mindset.
- Ability to recognize risk and change courses quickly.

Additional Information

- This position requires U.S. citizenship status.
- Internal Candidates must have adequate time in current role to apply
- Ability and willingness to sit on-site at the facility in Vandalia, OH.

The Wilmington site HR Leader is a key site leadership role responsible for aligning people strategy with business objectives for a 700+ employee manufacturing operation in Wilmington, NC.

This role partners closely with the Site Leader to lead the people priorities of the site strategy while driving workforce planning, talent development, employee relations, and organizational effectiveness across a workforce of ~550 hourly and ~150 salaried employees.

This position leads a team of two direct reports and partners across the site to support a high-performing, safe, and engaged culture. A strong focus of the role is strategic workforce planning and problem solving through FLIGHT DECK and Lean methodologies, enabling the site to execute at scale while developing and sustaining a workforce capable of meeting current and future business needs.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

- Lead strategic workforce planning for the site, including staffing plans, headcount forecasting, organizational design, succession planning, and capability development.
- Partner with the Site Leader and site leadership team to define and execute the people priorities that support the overall site strategy and business objectives.
- Lead and develop a team of two direct reports, ensuring accountability, capability building, and effective execution across HR priorities.
- Drive HR and business problem solving using FLIGHT DECK and Lean methodologies to improve performance, reduce variation, and support operational execution.

- Minimum 5 years prior experience in Human Resources, Business, Employee Relations or related area(s)

- Strong problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset
